Abilities.title: Abilities
Abilities.html:
Abilities are special features of some items and activities that cause effects when triggered. Ability cooldowns and charges are tracked globally for each activity so having multiple of the same ability granting item or pet only gives access to one instance of the ability. Each of the items, activities, or pets below grant the use of an ability but do not contain the ability itself.

Ability Types

  • Item Abilities
  • Active - These are abilities that are manually triggered by the player.
  • Consumable - These are consumable items that have a triggered ability. Currently this is only memopheres.
  • Activity Abilities
  • Activity - These are movement activities that teleport you to a new location on completion of an action.
  • Emergency - These are emergency activities that serve as anti-softlocks. They will teleport you to a safe location if you lack the necessary items to travel normally.
  • Pet Abilities
  • Active - These are abilities that are manually triggered by the player.
  • Passive - These are abilities that are always active generally to help with travel.

Item Abilities

Each item ability has the following parts.

  • Item Name: The item that grants the ability.
  • Effect: The result of activating the ability. Such as teleportation, completing actions, or creating items.
  • Requirement: What needs to happen to activate the ability. Such as being equipped, with you, or doing a specific type of activity.
  • Cooldown: How long before the ability can be used again. Such as completing a number of actions, or waiting an amount of time.
  • Charges: The number of stored uses the item has. You gain 1 charge per cooldown completed.
  • Note: Extra information about the ability.

Achievement_Points.title: Achievement Points
Achievement_Points.html:
Achievement Points are given for completing Achievements and obtaining Collectibles. Different difficulties of achievements will give different amounts of achievement points for completing them, and each collectible will give 1 achievement point.

Rewards

There are two types of awards that can be obtained from achievement points:

  • Total Progress Unlocks - You will gain these rewards based on your total progress in achievements, and you lose access to the items if more achievement points become available.
  • Check Point Unlocks - These achievements are available at certain achievement point checkpoints. You will not lose access to these even if more achievement points become available.

Activities.title: Activities
Activities.html:
There are a multitude of Activities that can be done in WalkScape throughout the world of Arenum.


When you select an activity, you begin completing actions of that activity until it no longer becomes possible to continue completing actions, or you select to do another activity. Actions are one completion of an activity, and reward things like experience, a chance at a chest, and create or transform materials.

There are roughly three categories of activities in the game:

  • Near-infinitely repeatable - Many gathering activities will produce an action every set number of steps until you tell your character to do something else. For example, if you select Cut pine trees as your activity, your character will continue chopping pine logs until you tell them to do otherwise. You will continue doing this activity at maximum efficiency until hitting the inventory soft-cap, or stopping when you are overencumbered - if you have the setting toggled on.
  • Finitely repeatable - Recipes and travelling activities generally produce a finite amount of possible actions. When selecting an activity such as Cut a Pine Plank, you can select how many actions you want to perform up to the maximum available based on the materials you have available to you, and the game will predict how many steps this will take you to complete. When travelling is your activity, your character will travel until reaching their destination.
  • Movement - These activities will cause you to appear in a different location after one action completed. This includes activities that are normally available like Venture into the bog as well as emergency escape activities that are anti-soft lock activities to make sure you aren't trapped in a location without the required gear to travel like Emergency swim escape.

Steps that you take while the game is active on your screen (foreground) are applied in real time to your current activity. If you close or background the game, the steps that you take will be immediately applied upon foregrounding the app or loading into the game.

Leveling a skill grants 1.25% Work Efficiency toward the attributed skill's activity up to a maximum of 25% or 20 levels above that of the required level to perform the activity.

Skills that can, will also benefit from a bonus of +1 Crafting Outcome per respective level beyond a Recipe's level requirement toward crafted items with no cap.


For activities involving multiple skills, the player is only eligible to earn chests in skills that have actual level requirements.

When performing an activity for a skill, only the primary skill is factored in for the player's equipment bonuses, the "2nd Skill" will also be affected by the equipment attributes based toward the "1st Skill" (IE: +1 Exp will apply to the "2nd Skill" as well).

Skills

Please see each skill's page to see their associated listed activities that we currently know of and where they can be done.

Adventurers'_Guild_Swampost.html:
Adventurers' Guild Swampost
Type: Outpost

The branch of the Adventurers' Guild attempting to keep the Halfmaw at bay. The key differences for this one are the dedicated name, a bit of redecorated layout with a large banking chest, along with the fact that it is a lot more green and run down than the one in Jarvonia. Also y'know, the swamp.

Adventurers' Guild Swampost is a "Outpost" building located in Halfmaw Hideout in the Grand Duchy of Trellin-Erdwise region.
It is home to the character Seth Kader.

Requirements

This building can only be entered if the following requirements have been met:

  • Have [10]Erdwise faction reputation.
  • Have [10]Halfling Rebels faction reputation.
  • Have [10]Trellin faction reputation.

Bank Options

This building allows you to deposit your items into the bank.
This building allows you to withdraw your items from the bank.

Agility.title: Agility
Agility.html:
Breathe in the fresh air while exercising in nature, adventuring through Arenum, and discovering treasures!

The Agilityskill is inherently linked to travelling between locations. You level up your agility simply by travelling, and the higher your level, the better agility equipment you can equip to travel faster. Equipment like Skis or the Grappling hook can change the steps required across different types of terrain. In the future, as you travel, you'll also encounter random events like small quests or interesting discoveries and pick up things along the way. You can also receive Agility chests as a rare drop from training this skill.

Travelling

Travelling is one of the main ways the player passively gains agility experience, as it is unavoidable activity for going places and playing the game. The amount of exp gained from travelling changes throughout leveling the skill. The amount of base steps changes for going to each location based on distances from one another (see all the routes here). The total amount of steps to get to the next closest location will get divided into 10 action nodes to fulfill, which will then count as the player arriving at that location.

In addition to the variation in experience gained from travelling, so does the chance to obtain Agility chests, which scales with the base steps required to reach a location instead of the base rate per action completion.

Travelling is unaffected by any penalties suffered from having an over-filled inventory.

There is no efficiency cap on the travelling activity. However there is a 100 step minimum between 2 locations (10 steps per node).

See Travelling (Mechanics) for more information on calculations for experience, chests, and efficiency.

Activities

The following activities can be done indefinitely without needing materials. Some have equipment requirements or other requirements that need to be satisfied in order to start the activity.

For activities involving two skills, the player is only eligible to earn chests in skills that have actual level requirements.

So, if the activity has a Agility level requirement, it will be eligible to drop Agility Chests.

When performing an activity for a skill, only the primary skill is factored in for the player's equipment bonuses, the "2nd Skill" will also be affected by the equipment attributes based toward the "1st Skill" (IE: +1 Exp will apply to the "2nd Skill" as well).

Anita_Lyfe.title: Anita Lyfe
Anita_Lyfe.html:
Anita Lyfe
Location:Lost Soulsourcing

A friendlier looking ghost that had lost their life in the floods. Perhaps they hold a way out of these ghostly lands through the barrier?

Anita Lyfe is a character who can be found at Lost Soulsourcing in Wraithwater in the Empire of Wallisia region.

Quote

  • Are you lost too? We all are here, but there can be comfort in some of the items of the material plane. Maybe you can help us through these exchanges.

Rumors

  • Dirty pirate.
  • Long ago, there had been a tale of a pirate here who had a prized Jar of dirt, of all the odd things to hold as a material joy. Lost in the floods to the north, perhaps some Flooded field scavenging can resurface it.
  • Shine by the shoreline.
  • A strange material thing to find to the south, along the shoreline, are the Shiny broken skydisc. Lost ones that speak of these say it splits the light itself against its surface.

Arctic Explorer
Type:Normal

You can call yourself a proud Jarvonian now, you know this land like your pocket.

Arctic Explorer is an achievement.

Requirement

  • Explore every location in Jarvonia[21]

Rewards

Achievement Point Rewards:

  • 3x achievement points

Other Rewards:

  • 3x Agility chest
  • Husky pup

Guides

  • Doing this will require having the Mysterious northern map and Black eye peak wilderness permit, which can be purchased from the Adventurers' Guild Outpost for 100 Adventurers' guild tokens each. 20 Achievement Points total are required to access the guild itself. Tokens can be best acquired by trading Adventurer Guild related materials obtained from specific Activities, which include Treasure hunt, Search team, and Rescue team.
  • The player also needs to visit Noiseless Pass which requires them to either purchase the Jarvonian letter of passage or to acquire the Diving Gear Set and make their way through Syrenthia.
  • Otherwise it is recommended to have Gear suited to Travelling for getting around the region itself.

Arenum.title: Arenum
Arenum.html:
The world of WalkScape is called Arenum. There is a lot going on in the ten regions of the world. Within each region, there are many activities and points of interest to consider such as:

  • Cities. Here you can visit NPC shops, refine your materials by using services like a forge, take on quests and so on.
  • Towns. Smaller than cities, but usually have similar features.
  • Forests. Foraging, woodcutting, hunting and combat options are usually available.
  • Mines. Mining and cave fishing options.
  • Dungeons. Usually contains lots of combat stuff.
  • Mountains. Mining and agility training options. Also might have combat and foraging options.
  • Beach/lake/river. Fishing options, limited woodcutting and foraging options.
  • And more!

World Map

Please see the Interactive World Map for a full screen view.

The In-Game Pixel Art Map of Arenum -

Older Pre-Beta Map of Arenum -

The Detailed Map of Arenum - Highlighted with Regions

Regions

Jarvonia

Jarvonia, a land of ice and darkness, ruled by a powerful religious brotherhood, is an independent realm of hardy people united by their unwavering faith and fierce determination to survive. Despite the harsh winters and isolation, they find strength and protection through their religion, their hearts burning bright against the cold.

  • Jarvonia is the starting region of the game. It hosts many woodcutting and fishingactivities, and is generally good for low level players.

Grand Duchy of Trellin-Erdwise

The Grand Duchy of Trellin-Erdwise (GDTE), divided in facing a current crisis, is a land of diverse natural beauty and challenges. The marshlands of Trellin and the coastal ports in Erdwise, are both sources of beauty and danger. The people of Trellin-Erdwise are defined by their pride and greed.

  • It connects the continent to Ewerethien. The old arena ruins has PvE content, and has a large variety of activities.

Syrenthia

The mini-realm of Syrenthia is home to the syrenthians. An underwater realm nested between Jarvonia, the Grand Duchy of Trellin-Erdwise, and the Empire of Wallisia.

Empire of Wallisia

Wallisia is a land of abundance and power. The Empress, a descendant of a great warrior, commands an army that has conquered the continent, leaving only Jarvonia untouched. The green grasslands are the heart of the whole continent, providing bountiful harvests as well as resources that fuel the empire's industrial and military capacities. The empire boasts the largest population in the continent, and the people are proud of their strength and power.

  • Wallisia hosts a Player-vs-Player arena, has fertile soil ripe for farming, and works as the main hub of the game.

Galeforge

Galeforge is a city of innovation and progress, conquered by the might of the Empire of Wallisia. Nestled between Wallisia and the archipelago, it is a place where technology and industry flourish. The people of Galeforge are ambitious and driven, constantly pushing boundaries of what's possible. The city is a bustling metropolis, where factories hum with activity and the streets are lined with merchants selling the latest innovations.

  • Galeforge grants access to a mysterious Archipelago, has high-tech innovation for sale, and hosts a variety of crafting opportunities.

Wrentmark

Wrentmark is a realm forged by fire, where the scorching sun beats down upon the desert sands. The people of Wrentmark are a proud and hardy lot, who have thrived in this harsh environment for ages. Wrentmark is a land of untold riches, where precious gems and minerals are mined from the earth and traded across the land. The people of Wrentmark are master merchants, their skills honed through centuries of commerce.

  • Wrentmark is a great place to mine minerals and gems, has a large variety of NPC shops, and hosts multiple guilds.

Painful Islands

The Painful Islands, a realm born out of tragedy and love. Created from the shattered remains of the Mana Deep Mountain, these desolate islands are home to monsters. But in the midst of this chaos lies a glimmer of hope. The Painful Islands may be a realm of terror, but is also a realm of determination and the relentless pursuit of redemption.

  • The Painful Islands are fantastic for combat focused players as it is filled with PvE content and dungeons. It is also home to special grotesque resources.

Ewerethien

Ewerethien, a realm of mystic wonder and arcane power. The land is blessed with magic, teeming with enchanted flora and fauna. The city of Academica stands tall, a beacon of knowledge and mastery of the arcane arts. A council of powerful mages, chosen for their skill and wisdom, rule from the heights of Whitescar Tower and drive forward their pursuit of greatness, enlightenment and research.

  • Ewerethien is home to the Mage's Guild, making it the ideal place to learn to use magic and gather magical items.

Braemercia

The rocky isle of Braemercia, home of the dwarves, rises from the tumultuous seas. For eons, the dwarves have delved deep into the earth, unearthing treasures untold from the Ironmouth Mine. But even the dwarves' unbroken spirit could not withstand the mages, who in their thirst for magrium, enslaved Bramercia's people and plundered the Ironmouth Mine.

  • Braemercia's deep mines contain high-end ores, has an NPC guild for miners, and hosts a variety of dwarven smiths who sell special items.

Rid Raddak

The lush jungles of Rid Raddak, the land of the elves, give way to the warm sands of the south. Once conquerors of the land, they now defend it against the monstrous hordes that threaten to overrun their realm. Though their cities may be in ruins, the spirit of the elves remains unbroken. The elves protect their home at all costs.

  • Rid Raddak is a huge continent with lots of content. Its Twilight Keep is a great place for PvE activities, mostly geared towards high level players.

Attributes.title: Attributes
Attributes.html:
Here's a list of the attributes you will see in game:

Bonus Experience

Changes the experience rewarded on action completion.

  • Mechanics Page
  • Items With This Attribute

Chest Finding

Changes the chance to find chests on action completion.

  • Mechanics Page

  • Items With This Attribute

Double Action

On completion, changes the chance for an action to give full rewards (experience and loot table rolls) twice. If this triggers when travelling - jump two nodes instead of one!

  • Mechanics Page
  • Items With This Attribute

Double Rewards

On completion, changes the chance for an action to give you two loot rolls instead of one.

  • Mechanics Page
  • Items With This Attribute

Find Bird Nests

Changes the chance to find Bird Nests on action completion.

  • Mechanics Page
  • Items With This Attribute

Find Collectibles

Changes the chance to find Collectibles on action completion.

  • Mechanics Page
  • Items With This Attribute

Find Gems

Changes the chance to find gems on action completion.

  • Mechanics Page
  • Items With This Attribute

Fine Material Finding

Changes the chance to find fine materials on action completion.

  • Mechanics Page
  • Items With This Attribute

Inventory Space

Adds additional maximum inventory spaces as long the item providing them is equipped.

  • Mechanics Page
  • Items With This Attribute

Item Finding

Adds a chance to find the specified object after every action.

  • Mechanics Page
  • Items With This Attribute

No Materials Consumed

Adds a chance to not use up the materials required for an activity that requires them.

  • Mechanics Page
  • Items With This Attribute

Quality Outcome

Changes the probabilities of getting higher quality crafted items.

  • Mechanics Page
  • Items With This Attribute

Steps Required

Removes the listed amount of steps from the activity you are doing, great if you have capped on work efficiency!

  • Mechanics Page
  • Items With This Attribute

Work Efficiency

Changes the value of work that your steps produce. Positive work efficiency decreases the amount of steps required to complete an action, while negative work efficiency increases the amount of steps required to complete an action.

  • Mechanics Page
  • Items With This Attribute

Banks.html:
A Bank is one of the basic types of buildings in the game. Banks can store an unlimited amount of any number of items.

This main function helps the player reduce the items in their inventory at once to prevent becoming overencumbered and resorting to dropping items.

Additionally, all banks are linked together and share a single bank inventory so you can deposit 1000 Pine logs in the Frozen Capital Bank in Kallaheim, Jarvonia. And then later withdrawal all 1000 from the Maritime Fortune Bank in Bilgemont Port, GDTE.

Functions at a Bank

When you are at a bank you currently have two options for what to do:

  • Deposit Items - Store items from your inventory into the bank.
  • You can store an unlimited amount, of unlimited types of items.
  • There is no fee or risk of losing items in the bank.
  • Long press the deposit button to store all of an item at once.
  • Depositing can also be done from your inventory when at a location with a bank, just long press an item stack to get the option to do so at the bottom-right of the screen.


  • Withdraw Items - Take items from the bank and put them into your inventory.
  • You are not limited with how many items you can take out at once, so Watch out for becoming overencumbered if withdrawing a lot of items.
  • Long press the withdraw button to take all of an item at once.

Checking Bank Inventory

You can check the items in your bank from anywhere by using the "Check Bank" button at the top of your inventory screen. This will let you view saved items, but you won't be able to withdraw or deposit unless the location you are at has a bank with those functions.

Checking Bank Statistics

You can check your bank statistics from inside the bank view by pressing the statistics button in the top row.

Bank Statistics Options

  • Credit Rating - See your total net worth and credit rating.

  • Gear & Tools by Rarity - See the total amount of each item rarity/quality you have in your bank and inventory.
  • Statistics - See your most valuable item, the total number of items owned, coins spent buying things, coins earned selling, and the net income from selling.

Barbantok.title: Barbantok
Barbantok.html:
Barbantok

Tucked away within a forest lies this town, carved out of the forest that encloses it. Fertile farmland and a chapel are noted when approaching. Many tree stumps are present on the edge of the woods.

Barbantok is a location that can be found in the Jarvonia region.

Bentley_Ward.title: Bentley Ward
Bentley_Ward.html:
Bentley Ward
Location:The Final Deposit

The young man in charge of the Blackrane bank. He is one of the many townspeople affected by the depressing blight upon them. It is hard to believe he will keep your items safe, but it looks he might value doing so more than his own life.

Bentley Ward is a character who can be found at The Final Deposit in Blackrane in the Empire of Wallisia region.

Quote

  • So you found time to make it to The Final Deposit? Can't say you made the right choice, but perhaps your stuff will still be safe even if you won't.

Rumors

  • No camel, no chance.
  • I'd give up hope of going the path southeast to Wrentmark if I were you. Unless you happen to have a camel with you there's no chance of surviving the harsh desert paths. Maybe you can luck out and find one at that fancy animal shelter we heard of up north in Salsfirth.
  • Lacking a net.
  • Sometimes I wish I could find a special Dragonfly catching net like the ones I heard people had before the war tore everything apart. The people back then apparently would just leave them out after they go Dragonfly catching. Maybe if I found one, I could have an excuse to get out of here.
  • Horned horrors.
  • People are sometimes foolish and head into the Stalking Yew Woods alone. They usually don't make it back, even with Swift sight goggles. It's vital they go with someone else to keep Unicorn hunting while they are there or they'll end up skewered.

Bert_Lamberen.title: Bert Lamberen
Bert_Lamberen.html:
Bert Lamberen
Location:Adventurers' Guild Outpost

The Adventurers' Guild representative for Jarvonia, Bert greets new worthy adventurers to the outpost. You can feel his warm welcoming presence but with an air of seriousness toward his duties.

Bert Lamberen is a character who can be found at Adventurers' Guild Outpost in Horn of Respite in the Jarvonia region.

Quote

  • Welcome fellow adventurer! I got a bank deposit box here for you to get stuff sent to your bank! Afraid I don't have a way to give you anything from your bank though. Feel free to join in on some search or rescue excursions if you are geared up! I'll give you tokens for items you find!

Rumors

  • Black Eye Peak?
  • Got a Black eye peak wilderness permit and looking to go Ridge scrambling up at Black Eye Peak? Be careful, bring some Climbing gear. I would recommend seeing if you can find a Mountaineering guidebook, though plenty of people I knew had one while doing that and still didn't make it back.
  • Spelunking venture.
  • What could be more exciting than exploring cavernous depths with some Spelunking up at Black Eye Peak?! Well, as long as you can come back in one piece of course, tough work bringing back just the remains of others sometimes. Though I suppose lots of people delve into those deep dark caverns in search of that lost civilization's Ancient ankh and other traces of its existence.
  • Bat cave to the south.
  • I've seen a lot of bats flying around that ruined trinketry bench tower far to the south of here. I bet if you peeked around in the cave over there for a bit, you could figure out where they migrate and maybe even follow them! You'd need a Black eye peak wilderness permit to get that way though! Should bring a few unique Light source options too!
  • Adventure to the north!
  • Hear that glacier up north has something worth exploring there! Would need to get your hands on a Mysterious northern map to probably find the way.
  • Lost treasure?
  • Nearby people have been reporting losing and finding items of importance in the area lately. Might be time to do a little Treasure hunt to see if you can turn up any of the lost items. Let's see, the rarest sounding item here. Ah, looks like someone lost their Artificial snowflake? I can only imagine how difficult that'd be to find in this snowy area.

Bonus_Experience.title: Bonus Experience
Bonus_Experience.html:
Bonus Experience is an attribute that changes the experience rewarded on action completion.

You may be looking for:

  • All the items with this attribute
  • How the game uses the attribute in calculations.
Bonus_Experience.text: Bonus Experience is an attribute that changes the experience rewarded on action completion. You may be looking for: All the items with this attribute How the game uses the attribute in calculations.

Bonus_Experience_(Mechanics).title: Bonus Experience (Mechanics)
Bonus_Experience_(Mechanics).html:
Bonus Experience Calculation

  1. Each activity has an initial base experience per action for each skill.
  2. Experience percentage bonuses from attributes is calculated. - The game only looks at the experience bonuses for equipment that affects the main skill for the activity. - These experience bonuses are applied to all skills that are used by the activity.
  3. Any flat experience given from an attribute is added.
  4. Percent bonuses are then added to the base 100% experience that you have for every activity.
  5. The base experience per action is multiplied by the calculated experience multiplier.
  6. The calculated total experience is then rounded down for display. - The game uses decimals for experience in the background with no rounding. You'll never lose or gain experience due to rounding errors.

Example with No Experience Bonuses

If we want to do Soup kitchen volunteering with no gear.

  1. We look at the base experience for the activity. - Soup Kitchen Volunteering has a base experience value of 24 experience points per action.
  2. We calculate any attribute bonuses (i.e. from equipment).
  3. We add the bonus flat bonus experience from attributes (i.e. from equipment). - We have no equipment that gives flat experience. = +0.0 experience - 24.00 experience points per action + 0.0 bonus experience = 24.00 total experience points per action - Equipment experience bonuses: We have no equipment that gives experience bonuses. = 0.00 added equipment experience
  4. We add the bonus experience to the base experience value. - 1.00 base experience multiplier + 0.00 equipment experience multiplier = 1.00 total experience multiplier
  5. We multiply the base experience per action by the calculated experience multiplier. - 24.00 base experience per action × 1.00 experience multiplier = 24.00 calculated experience per action
  6. We round the total experience per action down to the nearest full experience point for display. - 24.00 total experience per action rounds down to 24 displayed experience points per action

Example with Percent Experience Bonuses

If we want to do Soup kitchen volunteering with a Chef's hat.

  1. We look at the base experience for the activity. - Soup Kitchen Volunteering has a base experience value of 24 experience points per action.
  2. We calculate any attribute bonuses (i.e. from equipment).
  3. We add the bonus flat bonus experience from attributes (i.e. from equipment). - We have no equipment that gives flat experience. = +0.0 experience - 24.00 experience points per action + 0.0 bonus experience = 24.00 total experience points per action - Equipment experience bonuses: The Chef's Hat gives +6.0% bonus experience = 0.06 added equipment experience
  4. We add the bonus experience to the base experience value. - 1.00 base experience multiplier + 0.06 equipment experience multiplier = 1.06 total experience multiplier
  5. We multiply the base experience per action by the calculated experience multiplier. - 24.00 base experience per action × 1.06 experience multiplier = 25.44 calculated experience per action
  6. We round the total experience per action down to the nearest full experience point for display. - 25.44 total experience per action rounds down to 25 displayed experience points per action

Example with Flat Experience Bonuses

If we want to do Soup kitchen volunteering with an item giving flat bonus experience.

  1. We look at the base experience for the activity. - Soup Kitchen Volunteering has a base experience value of 24 experience points per action.
  2. We calculate any attribute bonuses (i.e. from equipment).
  3. We add the bonus flat bonus experience from attributes (i.e. from equipment). - Our item gives a +2.0 bonus experience. - 24.00 experience points per action + 2.0 bonus experience = 26.00 total experience points per action - Equipment experience bonuses: We have no gear that gives experience bonuses. = 0.00 added equipment experience
  4. We add the bonus experience to the base experience value. - 1.00 base experience multiplier + 0.00 equipment experience multiplier = 1.00 total experience multiplier
  5. We multiply the base experience per action by the calculated experience multiplier. - 26.00 base experience per action × 1.00 experience multiplier = 26.00 calculated experience per action
  6. We round the total experience per action down to the nearest full experience point for display. - 26.00 total experience per action rounds down to 26 displayed experience points per action

Example with Experience Bonuses and an Activity with Multiple Skills Requirements

If we want to do Firewood making with a Lumberjack shirt.

  1. We look at the base experience for the activity. - Firewood Making has a base experience value of:
    • 15 experience points per action for woodcutting
    • 10 experience points per action for agility.
  2. We calculate any attribute bonuses (i.e. from equipment).
  3. We add the bonus flat bonus experience from attributes (i.e. from equipment). - The Lumberjack Shirt gives a +1.0 bonus experience.
    • Woodcutting: 15.00 experience points per action + 1.0 bonus experience = 16.00 total experience points per action
    • Agility: 10.00 experience points per action + 1.0 bonus experience = 11.00 total experience points per action
    • Equipment experience bonuses: The Lumberjack Shirt gives +6.0% bonus experience when woodcutting = 0.06 added equipment experience
  4. We add the bonus experience to the base experience value. - Woodcutting: 1.00 base experience multiplier + 0.06 equipment experience multiplier = 1.06 total experience multiplier - Agility: 1.00 base experience multiplier + 0.06 equipment experience multiplier = 1.06 total experience multiplier
  5. We multiply the base experience per action by the calculated experience multiplier. - Woodcutting: 16 base experience per action × 1.06 experience multiplier = 16.96 calculated experience per action - Agility: 11 base experience per action × 1.06 experience multiplier = 11.66 calculated experience per action
  6. We round the total experience per action down to the nearest full experience point for display. - Woodcutting: 16.96 total experience per action rounds up to 17 displayed woodcutting experience points per action - Agility: 11.66 total experience per action rounds up to 12 displayed agility experience points per action

Note: The game tracks the full decimal value for experience so you are not gaining an extra 0.04 from woodcutting or 0.34 from agility in this example.

Borus_Caskelair.title: Borus Caskelair
Borus_Caskelair.html:
Borus Caskelair
Location:Gold'n Grail Blackspell

The Caskelair brother responsible for the Gold'n Grail Tavern branch in Blackspell Harbour. He looks wise, but maybe it is just a facade. Although the confidence coming from him is real.

Borus Caskelair is a character who can be found at Gold'n Grail Blackspell in Blackspell Harbour in the Grand Duchy of Trellin-Erdwise region.

Quote

  • Hey! Welcome to the good Gold'n Grail! Take a seat! Can I get you some fresh wine? Nothing beats it! See my brothers at any other locations yet? They tell the best stories!

Rumors

  • Horus has great peppy stories!
  • My good brother Horus! He's over at the Gold'n Grail in Everhaven! You gotta pay him a visit! There's a nice girl over that area too at the Breeze Mart, she loves hearing Horus tell a good story. She sells some cool stuff too. I've seen a Simple magnet and Simple bug catching net. Bet you could use them for some fun activities!
  • Morus tells great spooky stories!
  • Good brother Morus! He's over there trying his best at the Gold'n Grail in Bilgemont Port, even though he says he hates it! He'll do anything to help and has a keen eye! He even helped be an Antique market assessor over here for a bit, even found a Meteorite fragment in the collection! Though I heard there might be a few more hiding out there.
  • Ship it!
  • There's some good views down by the docks! The ships over here always need Hull repair, feels like the area always has a Sailor's hat somewhere. Sure is a lot of interesting language used around there.

Trivia

  • The first letters of each of the Caskelair brothers together come out to be HMB (Hold My Beer) to suit their tavern jobs.

Carpentry.title: Carpentry
Carpentry.html:
Process raw logs into components of precise measurement to craft useful items with.

The Carpentryskill is primarily used to process material like logs into planks, and later on, the plan is to include building farm buildings. With higher carpentry levels, you'll have access to more logs and special skilling equipment that can boost your carpentry efficiency. You can also receive Carpentry Chests as a rare drop from training this skill.

Activities

The following activities can be done indefinitely without needing materials. Some have equipment requirements or other requirements that need to be satisfied in order to start the activity.

For activities involving two skills, the player is only eligible to earn chests in skills that have actual level requirements.

So, if the activity has a Carpentry level requirement, it will be eligible to drop Carpentry Chests.

When performing an activity for a skill, only the primary skill is factored in for the player's equipment bonuses, the "2nd Skill" will also be affected by the equipment attributes based toward the "1st Skill" (IE: +1 Exp will apply to the "2nd Skill" as well).

A massive shipwreck lies in the sand. Who knows how long it's been here? Some fish and other creatures have taken it as their home. Colourful underwater plants grow on the shipwreck and around it, creating a spectacular sight.

Casbrant's Grave is a location that can be found in the Syrenthia region.

Character Experience Function

/// Calculates the experience needed to level up character level
double xpToLevelCharacter(int level) {
  double xp = 0;
  for (var i = 1; i < level + 1; i++) {
    xp += xpEquate(i.toDouble());
  }
  return (xp / 4).floor().toDouble() * 4.6;
}

/// XP equation algorithm
int xpEquate(double level) {
  return (level + 300 * pow(2, level / 7)).floor();
}

Explanation

The 'xpToLevelCharacter' Function

  • Accepts an integer 'level' as input.
  • Initializes 'xp' to 0.
  • Iterates through all levels from 1 up to the target 'level'.
  • For each level, it calculates the XP required using the 'xpEquate' function and accumulates it in 'xp'.
  • Divides the total XP by 4, rounds it down, and then multiplies the result by 4.6 to produce the final XP value needed for the specified level.

The 'xpEquate' Function

  • Accepts a level as a 'double'.
  • Calculates the XP required for that specific level using the equation:
  • XP = level + 300 × 2(level ÷ 7)
  • Rounds down the result to return an integer value.

Chest_Finding.text: Chest Finding is an attribute that changes the chance to find Chests on action completion. You may be looking for: All the items with this attribute How the game uses the attribute in calculations.

Chest_Finding_(Mechanics).title: Chest Finding (Mechanics)
Chest_Finding_(Mechanics).html:
Chest Finding Calculation

  1. Most activities have a roll on one or more chest tables. - In general, an activity that has a skill with a level requirement has a chance to give a chest for that skill.
  2. Chest finding percentage bonuses from attributes is calculated.
  3. These bonuses are added to the base chest finding multiplier that you have.
  4. The base chest drop chance (.4% or 1/250) is multiplied by the calculated chest finding multiplier.
  5. The modified chest finding odds are rolled on a loot table.

Note that we can quickly get a value by simply adding the total percent chest finding to 1 and dividing by 250.

Example with No Chest Finding Bonuses

If we want to go Forest foraging with no equipment, and we complete a foraging action.

  1. Forest foraging is able to give a Foraging chest roll in its loot tables.
  2. We have no equipment, so we have no percent chest finding bonus. - Chest finding bonus = 0.00
  3. We added our chest finding bonus to the base chest finding multiplier that you have. - 1.00 chest finding multiplier + 0.00 chest finding bonus = 1.00 calculated chest finding multiplier
  4. We multiply the base chest drop chance by the calculated chest finding multiplier. - 0.004 × 1.00 = 0.004 modified chest finding odds
  5. The modified chest finding odds are rolled on a loot table. - Our 0.004 modified chest finding odds gives us a 1/250 chance per action completed to receive a Foraging chest.

Example with a Chest Finding Bonus

If we want to go Forest foraging with a good quality Steel sickle, and we complete a foraging action.

  1. Forest foraging is able to give a Foraging chest roll in its loot tables.
  2. Our good Steel sickle gives a +13.0% chest finding - Chest finding bonus = 0.13
  3. We added our chest finding bonus to the base chest finding multiplier that you have. - 1.00 chest finding multiplier + 0.13 chest finding bonus = 1.13 calculated chest finding multiplier
  4. We multiply the base chest drop chance by the calculated chest finding multiplier. - 0.004 × 1.13 = 0.00452 modified chest finding odds
  5. The modified chest finding odds are rolled on a loot table. - Our 0.00452 modified chest finding odds gives us a 1.13/250 chance per action completed to receive a Foraging chest.

Chests.title: Chests
Chests.html:
Opening a Foraging chest from the Treasury.

Chests are openable items that drop at a base 1/250 rate per action from doing activities (with the exception of travelling). Their type is determined by the activity's skills involved that have actual level requirements and not the experience obtained. This can lead to some activities having the potential to drop more than one chest type in a single action. If an activity can drop more than one chest or openable, they each have an independent 1/250 base drop rate as well.

When acquired, they do not take up space, but instead they will be displayed in your treasury tab under your Inventory where they can be viewed or opened from there. The rewards for a chest are rolled upon opening, not upon receiving the chest.

The Chest Finding equipment attribute can add to the base drop rate of finding chests during activities. So equipment with "+1%Chest Finding" gives a new chance of 1.01/250 per roll on the chest loot table (does not affect the ability to find Bird Nests).

While uniquely, the Find Bird Nests equipment attribute can add to the base 1/250 drop rate of finding Bird Nests during their obtainable activities in the same manner.

Loot Rolls

All chests go through four rolls for loot. Each of those rolls gets broken up into two separate rolls. The first part of a roll goes based on the table below. After rolling on that, it will then roll for an item based on the sub-table involved.

If a chest has a sub-table or tables that are blank the games adds that chance onto the miscellaneous table's chances.

Please note that the chances for loot are based off of the individual rolls and not the total amount given by a chest/treasury item itself.

Coins.title: Coins
Coins.html:
Coins
Type:Currency

Coins are the currency of WalkScape.

Currently the uses for coins are quite limited. Coins are generally used to purchase materials or equipment from the various shops across Arenum. However, to travel outside of the starting area of Jarvonia, a player is required to purchase a Jarvonian letter of passage. This special collectible item costs 4.5K coins and grants the player further access to the world map through the GDTE.

Once player-to-player trading is added, coins will play a more important role as it will be essential for the player based economy to function.

Type: Bank

A very clean-looking bank that somehow keeps free of the outside snow. You would swear you are looking through blue-tinted lenses, as even the torches here burn blue. Only those that are highly respected by the Jarvonians can enter such a space.

Cold Storage of Commitment is a "Bank" building located in Azurazera in the Jarvonia region.
It is home to the character Elara Frostledger.

Requirement

This building can only be entered if the following requirement has been met:

Collectibles.title: Collectibles
Collectibles.html:
Collectibles are special items that require no inventory space and get added automatically once found under your Character icon > Achievements > Special Items > Collectibles. If they have an effect, it will be applied permanently to your character. They cannot be sold or stack once obtained, so obtaining more than one gives no benefits. When obtained from an activity, they drop from their own table, and thus do not take away other drop opportunities. Each collectible also grants 1 Achievement Point helping you to progress towards rewards and unlocks.

Consumables.title: Consumables
Consumables.html:
Consumables are items made typically via cooking skill recipes or obtained through other activities and chests.

To use a consumable on an activity, you must be "using" enough of them to complete the action of the activity in steps.
Example: Doing a single action of Rescue team, where it ends up taking you personally 5667 steps to complete, would require 6 Jelly sandwiches (6 x 1000 for 6000 steps of coverage).

Cooking.title: Cooking
Cooking.html:
Carefully select natural ingredients and turn them into delicious feasts that will make stomachs rumble and mouths water.

The Cookingskill allows you to prepare consumables which can give temporary skilling boosts. Some recipes are simple (like cooking fish) while others are more complex, requiring many materials. With higher cooking levels, you'll have access to more cooking ingredients, better recipes, and special skilling equipment that can boost your cooking efficiency. You can also receive Cooking Chests as a rare drop from training this skill.

Activities

The following activities can be done indefinitely without needing materials. Some have equipment requirements or other requirements that need to be satisfied in order to start the activity.

For activities involving two skills, the player is only eligible to earn chests in skills that have actual level requirements.

So, if the activity has a Cooking level requirement, it will be eligible to drop Cooking Chests.

When performing an activity for a skill, only the primary skill is factored in for the player's equipment bonuses, the "2nd Skill" will also be affected by the equipment attributes based toward the "1st Skill" (IE: +1 Exp will apply to the "2nd Skill" as well).

Core_Mechanics.title: Core Mechanics
Core_Mechanics.html:
Welcome to WalkScape!

Simplified Core Gameplay Loop

Walk for In-Game Progress

In WalkScape, in-game progress happens as you step in real life. Steps are counted by the pedometer on your phone and applied in real time to the game.

The core gameplay loop revolves around selecting a skill activity (e.g. chopping pine logs, ocean fishing, crafting iron axes, travelling to another location in the game), and taking a certain number of steps to complete that action. Once you complete an action, you gain materials, coins, and if you are lucky - even chests or other rare drops. Your character then begins the action again if it is possible. This continues until you select a new activity in-game.

If it is no longer possible to continue your action in-game (e.g. you run out of materials, you reach your destination in-game, etc.) and you are still taking steps in real life, there is a small buffer called Saved Steps (sometimes also referred to as the "Step Bank") that will become charged. Once you select a new activity, one step from the step bank will apply to your current activity for each step you take in life. So, if you stored 3000 steps in the step bank by being idle in-game, the next 3000 steps in real life will be doubled in-game. The Saved Steps are a limited resource whose size grows with character level, so it's best to pay attention to how long you can do various activities.

Skills

There are 10 skills in the WalkScape: Agility, Carpentry, Cooking, Crafting, Foraging, Fishing, Mining, Smithing, Trinketry and Woodcutting. Head over to the skills page to learn more. Skills are trained by activities in game.

Character Level

In addition to skills, your account has an overall Character Level. This level describes the total number of steps you have taken over your account lifetime, and is important for some types of overall account progression such as unlocking toolbelt slots and increasing the saved steps maximum.

Items

There are many types of items in WalkScape:

  • Crafted. These are typically obtained mainly by crafting them yourself or buying one that's been crafted by someone else.
  • Loot. You can gain loot from shops, chests, dead enemies, randomly from some activities, quest rewards and so forth.
  • Equipment. Is divided up into gear and tools, that can be equipped to your character. They will be either Crafted or Loot themselves too.
  • Material. They're what's used to craft other items. Pretty self explanatory.
  • Consumables. They're things like potions and food which can be consumed to heal yourself or to gain a buff.
  • Treasury. They do not need an inventory space and can be opened. These contain other items.
  • Quest. These don't need an inventory space and are used in quests to progress.
  • Collectibles. These do not take up inventory space and are always with your character.

Achievements

The Closed Beta Test currently contains over 70 achievements. Getting half of the achievement points in the game will earn the player a Cape of Half-Achiever, and getting all of the achievement points will earn the player the Cape of Achiever.

Cosmetics.title: Cosmetics
Cosmetics.html:
Cosmetics are options to change the look of your character in Walkscape! Cosmetics have no in game use beside their visuals.

Cosmetics come in two types.

  • Clothing and things your character wears can be Outfits, Headwear, and Face, Back, and Eye accessories. Most of these can be purchased in a clothing store like Tundra Trends.
  • The look of your character can be Faces, Noses, Hairstyles, and Facepaint as well as the color options for each. These can modified at a barber shop like Polar Pruning.

Crafted_Items.title: Crafted Items
Crafted_Items.html:
Crafted Items are items such as tools, weapons, shields and other equipment made by the player through the use of the Transformation skills.

A tool crafting screen, with quality chances shown under the 'Rewards' section.

Quality

Similar to Loot Items, they also come in 6 increasingly better forms of quality:

Crafted QualityIn-Game ColorTagSmall
Tag
NormalGrey
GoodGreen
GreatBlue
ExcellentPurple
PerfectGold
EternalRed

Each higher level of quality will add a new attribute to the item. Attributes are predetermined based on the tier of item. For example, every "Great" Iron pickaxe will have the same stats: the base attribute that comes with the "normal" quality, plus 2 additional attributes.

Your chances to craft higher quality items will increase with skill level, equipment, buffs, and the use of fine materials.

Crafting Tiers

The qualities of crafted items and the tier of materials interact to create overlapping overall usefulness called the Gear Score Index (GSI). This chart by floursifter shows the comparison of qualities and GSI for each tier of crafted gear (Pickaxes and Hatchets are represented in this chart.)

Crafting.title: Crafting
Crafting.html:
Combine components with your endless creativity and craftsmanship to produce artisanal tools and equipment.

The Craftingskill allows you to create tools like fishing rods, pickaxes, and hatchets which are needed to train other skills. Tools can be crafted in six different qualities and using fine materials will increase your chances of making a higher quality tool. With higher crafting levels, you'll be able to use more materials to make better tools as well as use special skilling equipment that can boost your crafting efficiency. You can also receive Crafting chests as a rare drop from training this skill.

Activities

The following activities can be done indefinitely without needing materials. Some have equipment requirements or other requirements that need to be satisfied in order to start the activity.

For activities involving two skills, the player is only eligible to earn chests in skills that have actual level requirements.

So, if the activity has a Crafting level requirement, it will be eligible to drop Crafting Chests.

When performing an activity for a skill, only the primary skill is factored in for the player's equipment bonuses, the "2nd Skill" will also be affected by the equipment attributes based toward the "1st Skill" (IE: +1 Exp will apply to the "2nd Skill" as well).

Type:Container
Keyword:Chest

While you were crafting your creations, you noticed this big red toolbox was suddenly next to your own tools.

Crafting chest is an openable treasury item. It can drop while doing Crafting activities, and can be obtained from some other sources. These Chests are the only way to obtain some Crafting based Equipment. They can have the odds of finding them increased with the Chest Findingequipmentattribute.

Currencies.title: Currencies
Currencies.html:
Currency items are non-inventory items that are stored in the currency tab of your character. They are used to buy items from most Shops. Currency items can be separated into Gold coins, Chest chips, and Guild Tokens.

Gold Coins

Gold coins are the primary currency in Walkscape they can be obtained by selling items to shops as well as directly from activities or coin pouches.

Chest Chips

Chest Chips are the currency used by the Mysterious Merchant. You can sell chest loot items for their corresponding chip, and use the chips to buy chest loot items.

Chip NameChest Source
Agility chipAgility chest
Carpentry chipCarpentry chest
Cooking chipCooking chest

Syrenthia chipChest of Syrenthia
Halfling Rebels chipChest of the Halfling Rebels

Guild Tokens

Guild Tokens are the currency used by the Adventurers' Guild. You can sell some items at the outposts for tokens as well as get them from an attribute.

Double_Action.title: Double Action
Double_Action.html:
Double Action is an attribute that changes the chance for an action to be completed twice instead of once, giving full rewards (experience and loot table rolls) twice. If this triggers when travelling - jump two nodes instead of one!

You may be looking for:

  • All the items with this attribute
  • How the game uses the attribute in calculations.

If this triggers when travelling - jump two nodes instead of one! You may be looking for: All the items with thi

Double_Action_(Mechanics).title: Double Action (Mechanics)
Double_Action_(Mechanics).html:
Double Action Calculation

  1. Double action has a chance to occur on every activity completion except those resulting from Double action itself. - Note: This means that you cannot get an endless string of Double action activations, only one per real action.
  2. Double action percentage bonuses from attributes is calculated.
  3. The Double action percentage chance is rolled to see if it occurs on this action. - Note: This attribute has a cap of 100% which would result in a Double action for every action.

Example with No Double Action Bonus

If we want to craft a Steel pickaxe with no equipment, and we complete a crafting action.

  1. Craft a Steel pickaxe has two drop tables one for the pickaxe itself and another for a crafting chest.
  2. We have no equipment, so we have no double action percentage. - Double action = 0.00
  3. Our 0.00 double action odds gives us a 0% chance per action completed. - We will not get any double actions. - We receive one pickaxe roll for quality and one crafting chest roll as normal.
    • The pickaxe drops as a Good Steel pickaxe

Example with a Double Action Bonus

If we want to craft a Steel pickaxe with a Magnifying lens, and we complete a crafting action.

  1. Craft a Steel pickaxe has two drop tables one for the pickaxe itself and another for a crafting chest.
  2. Magnifying lens gives 5% bonus to double action. - Double action = 0.05
  3. Our 0.05 double action odds gives us a 5% chance per action completed. - We roll for double action at the completion of the action and get it. - We use up two sets of materials for crafting a steel pickaxe and receive two pickaxes and two chances for chests.
    • The first pickaxe rolls its quality and is dropped as a Normal Steel pickaxe
    • The second pickaxe rolls its quality and is dropped as a Good Steel pickaxe.
    • We roll on the chest loot table twice.
    • We do the first chest roll according to Chest Finding (Mechanics) but don't happen to receive a crafting chest.
    • We do the second chest roll and receive a Crafting chest.

Note that this is exactly the same as completing an action twice normally. This is similar in some ways to the Double Rewards Mechanic except it gives experience and progress as well. They can work well together though. Double action gives twice the chance for double rewards to occur so in rare chances you can have four loot rolls from one completed action. See below for more information.

Example with a Double Action Bonus while Travelling

If we want to travel from Kallaheim to Frusenholm with an Exercise headband, and we complete node in the travel action.

  1. Kallaheim to Frusenholm has 10 nodes between it, we've walked the steps for the first tenth of the distance.
  2. Exercise headband gives 15% bonus to double action only when travelling. - Double action = 0.15
  3. Our 0.15 double action odds gives us a 15% chance per action completed. - We roll for double action at the completion of the action and get it. - We complete two travelling actions.
    • The first action moves us 1/10 of the way to Frusenholm
    • The second action moves us an additional 1/10 of the distance, for a total of 2/10 of the distance for 1 actions work of work.
    • We roll on the chest loot table twice.
    • We do the first chest roll according to Chest Finding (Mechanics) and receive an Agility chest.
    • We do the second chest roll and receive a second Agility chest.

Interactions Between Double Action, Double Rewards and No Materials Consumed

Let's first go over the high level of what each attribute does especially in the context of transformation recipes. I will use the abbreviation DA for Double Action, DR for Double Rewards and NMC for No Materials Consumed.

  • DA works by triggering a second action for 0 steps, this rolls all tables again, awards Skill XP, and can re-trigger all attributes except DA itself.
  • DR works by re-rolling all loot tables again, this includes main/recipe outcome, chests, collectibles, etc. Importantly each roll (both first and DR induced) can have separate outcomes and are independent of each other.
  • NMC works by not consuming materials for a recipe action. Those items still stayed queued for further recipes. On non-recipe activities NMC has no effect.

The basic flow of a crafting action is:

  1. You walk until the steps are reduced to 0.
  2. An action is triggered.
  3. Attributes are checked: - The check for NMC occurs and if it procs you do not use a recipe input. - The check for DR occurs and if it procs you roll loot tables twice. - The check for DA occurs and if it procs then you go back to step 2 for a new action skipping the check for DA on the second action.
  4. Sum and display results.

This results in the following possible outcomes:

Double_Rewards.html:
Double Rewards is an attribute that changes the chance for an action to give two loot table rolls instead of one.

You may be looking for:

  • All the items with this attribute

Double_Rewards.text: Double Rewards is an attribute that changes the chance for an action to give two loot table rolls instead of one. You may be looking for: All the items with this attribute How the game uses the attribute in calculations.

Double_Rewards_(Mechanics).title: Double Rewards (Mechanics)
Double_Rewards_(Mechanics).html:
Double Rewards Calculation

  1. Double rewards has a chance to occur on every activity completion.
  2. Double rewards percentage bonuses from attributes is calculated.
  3. The Double rewards percentage chance is rolled to see if it occurs on this action. - Note: This attribute has a cap of 100% which would result in a Double rewards for every action.

Example with No Double Rewards Percentage

If we want to go Lake fishing with no equipment, and we complete a fishing action.

  1. Lake fishing has two drop tables one for fish and another for a fishing chest.
  2. We have no equipment, so we have no double rewards percentage. - Double rewards percentage = 0.00
  3. Our 0.00 double rewards odds gives us a 0% chance per action completed. - We will not get any double rewards. - We receive one fish loot table roll and one fishing chest roll as normal.

Example with a Double Rewards Bonus

If we want to go Litter looting with a Pointy shears, and we complete a foraging action.

  1. Litter looting has two drop tables one for items and another for a foraging chest.
  2. Pointy shears gives 2% bonus to double rewards - Double rewards percentage = 0.02
  3. Our 0.02 double rewards odds gives us a 2% chance per action completed. - We roll for our double rewards and get it.
    • We receive 1 stone from the first roll and 1 Smelly Socks from the second roll on the main drops table.
    • We do the first chest roll according to Chest Finding (Mechanics) but don't happen to receive a foraging chest, we do the second chest roll and receive a Foraging chest.

Note that each loot table is rolled twice but each roll is independent for what loot you receive. This is very similar to the Double Action Mechanic but only gives the second loot table roll. They can work well together though. Double action gives twice the chance for double rewards to occur so in rare chances you can have four loot rolls from one completed action. See below for more information.

Earth_Day_Cleanup.title: Earth Day Cleanup
Earth_Day_Cleanup.html:
Description

(Taken from Walkscape Discord Server)

The Earth Day is 22th of April, so in just a couple of days from now and we would like to celebrate it by doing a small test event. After the game is out, we would like to do similar events within the game.

WalkScape is very much related to walking outside. And while walking outside, seeing bunch of trash is quite nasty. So in the theme of Earth Day, participants of this event will be ranked based on how many garbage bags they can plog.

To participate in the event, you need to take a picture of filled bags and post it here on ⁠event or on Twitter by mentioning @WalkScape. Doing this on Twitter helps us, so if you feel like sharing this there, it would be awesome! If you do multiple plogging runs during the event, mention or link your previous entry in the most recent one, so we can follow the chain of links from the most recent one.

As a guideline, use 25L bags that are filled so that they can still be closed fully. If you use bigger bags, they don't have to be as full. That's ~6.6 gallons in imperial units.

Important: Include a note with the date and WalkScape in your pictures.

I hope to see a lot of filled up bags, let's make our neighborhoods cleaner together!

Rewards

Top 1 : Design a special item to WalkScape with the team and have your name in its description.

Top 3 : A Profile picture made by maxchill.

Top 5 : Guaranteed closed beta spot. Yeah, a juicy reward for your hard work!

1+ bags : A special Discord role to show off your efforts in this event. 5 guaranteed closed beta spots will also be randomly distributed to participants who meet this requirement.

Empire_of_Wallisia.title: Empire of Wallisia
Empire_of_Wallisia.html:
The Empire of Wallisia is located south of the GDTE and hosts the capital for the entirety of the Western Continent of Arenum. It operates as the main hub of the game.

It is a land of abundance and power. The Empress, a descendant of a great warrior, commands an army that has conquered the continent, leaving only Jarvonia untouched. The green grasslands are the heart of the whole continent, providing bountiful harvests as well as resources that fuel the empire's industrial and military capacities. The empire boasts the largest population in the continent, and the people are proud of their strength and power.

Locations

  • Urban Areas
  • Wraithwater
  • Blackrane
  • Other areas
  • Tendon Wet Fields
  • Kildome Cross
  • Stalking Yew Woods
  • Blackwater Fields
  • Blackwater Lake

Quests

TBD.

History

Arenum's timeline can be divided into two parts: before the Arena and after it.

Prior to the Arena, the population, particularly in the West, was constantly at war. After the Wallisians conquered Wrentmark, Galeforge, and GDTE, the reigning emperor decided to construct the arena as a memorial to his victory but also as a sign of future wars being resolved in a different, although still violent, manner. The Arena provided a place where two or more parties could settle their grievances without involving the general population.

Arena is still very popular in the West, and it is also frequented by fighters and spectators from all of the other fantasy races in the East. There is also a period of calm and stability. The Arena has been seen as a symbol of unity in a region previously divided by war and animosity.

Government and politics

The Empress currently rules Wallisia. The Empress is already old, and Wallisia's main story will be about the succession issue she thinks will occur after her death. She wants to maintain the empire intact, which may be impossible if a severe crisis happens. GDTE, Wrentmark, and Galeforge may seek independence once more. She has three sons: oldest one feels that he is destined to join the religion in Jarvonia, and then the younger twins might battle for the throne, making the whole succession process a disaster.

The aged Empress of Wallisia was feeling her mortality and the impending end of her reign. Her ailing heart weighed heavy with the knowledge that she had to find a solution to keep her empire from collapsing in chaos after her death. With multiple factions tensions escalating, she knew it would be difficult.

The Empress had three sons: an eldest whose curiosity for the religion in Jarvonia had shifted his interests away from taking the throne; then there was a set of younger twins who each coveted the title of emperor. The siblings' rivalry for the crown caused a palpable tension within the palace walls.

What was to become of the Empress and her vast empire? The looming succession crisis that hung over the royal family was feared to have only one resolution: a massacre that would end any hopes of preserving her father's dynasty.

Ernie_Lamperen.title: Ernie Lamperen
Ernie_Lamperen.html:
Ernie Lamperen
Location:Tool Market Stall

The market stall holds a rather stout human behind it, organizing some of the tools that are neatly laid out. His hair is hidden by a large brown fishing hat, his beard is neatly trimmed as well. A shy, timid smile is offered.

Ernie Lamperen is a character who can be found at Tool Market Stall in Granfiddich in the Grand Duchy of Trellin-Erdwise region.

Quote

  • O-oh! Goodness, you scared me a little. Do you need some tools? I know most adventurers make their own, but it doesn't hurt to have extras, right? I'm Ernie by the way, Ernie Lamperen.

Rumor

  • Super soup volunteer.
  • The Eberhart Mansion Kitchen (Advanced) always needs local Soup kitchen volunteering help. I heard people that stand out helping even get a Soup kitchen badge to give them access to their prestigious kitchen for their own personal benefit! Though it still means dealing with all the other people using it at the same time I guess.

FAQs.title: FAQs
FAQs.html:
Please visit https://walkscape.app/help for some other Frequently Asked Questions!

Also, view the included video for getting help with getting access/fully connected with WalkScape!

What is WalkScape?

: WalkScape is an RPG game inspired by RuneScape and other MMORPGs. However, it has one glaring difference: you don't play it actively. Instead, you gain progress by walking in real life. The game has a massive open-world map with over a hundred locations for the player to explore. The world is filled with lore, NPCs, quests, and activities for the player to engage in, and more! Our goal with the game is to encourage an active lifestyle and promote both mental and physical health.

App Related

How can I get the game?

: WalkScape is in closed beta, which means you need to be invited to play. We invite players who have filled out an application as we need new testers. The queue times vary, but most players get an invite after a few months. You are guaranteed an instant invite to the game if you have supported the project on Patreon or Buy Me a Coffee.

When will the game leave closed beta status?

: The Closed Beta Test is currently ongoing. WalkScape plans to leave closed beta once we have the following missing features:

  • Trading
  • Quests
  • Combat

No earlier than Q4 2026.

Will my progress get reset after the closed beta testing ends?

: Yes, there is a planned wipe during the transition from closed beta to open beta testing. It's possible but not yet confirmed if you will be able to keep your closed beta character as a offline single player character.

Does the game require GPS?

: No, the game uses your phone's pedometer. You can play the game stepping in place, walking around your house, on a treadmill, while shopping for groceries. Play where you feel safe.

How will the game register that a player walks?

: The game uses your device's step sensor data. Each modern phone these days track your steps automatically, and the game currently uses that data to determine how many steps you've gained. Currently iOS users can use Apple Heath to utilize their smart watches as an alternative option. Android users can use a variety of 3rd party smartwatches along with Samsung health integration. This way, smart watches are also something you could use to gain steps in-game and are a top priority to get working further.

Will there be a bike mode?

: The Devs have talked about this internally, and they are totally for this idea eventually. Conversion rate would still be made so cycling or other activities are not superior to walking.

On what platforms will WalkScape be released?

: The game is available through Google Play Store (Android) and Testflight (iOS).

What is the future monetization strategy of the game?

: Offline mode - One time purchase. You’ll be able to pay once to download the offline mode of the game. You’ll receive future content updates, not have a requirement to be online to open the game, and have a slider that multiplies your steps to reach the game experience that you wish. No multiplayer features.

: Online mode - affordable monthly subscription. You’ll need to be online to play the game, but you’ll receive future content updates and all multiplayer features that the game has to offer.

: Free to play area - both forms of the game will have a free to play area that can be enjoyed for free.

I've got a new phone, how can I transfer my progress?

: By default, your characters and progress are saved to the cloud, but it's a good idea to check that your progress is saved before moving over. Playing the game on two devices is also against the rules, so to make sure that you're not flagged by anti-cheat, you should delete the game on your old device, before opening it on the new one. Here are the steps to do that:

  1. Open the game on your old device. If you head over to the leaderboards and your stats match the ones on your skill screen, you know that progress has been saved to the cloud.
  2. Close the game and uninstall it.
  3. Install the game on the new device using the same instructions as before. Login with your Portal credentials.

: Note: iOS and some Android distributions provide automatic app transfers, but WalkScape isn't yet compatible with these and will require a reinstall in most cases.

How often do I need to open the game to not lose steps?

: A good rule of thumb is to open the game every 7 days. Depending on your platform, step source (wearable vs phone) and other factors beyond our control, steps can be loaded from 10-30 days in the past, but these can vary. Opening the game once every week should prevent you from losing any steps, though.

Are you guys in search of translators?

: The Devs appreciate translation help! You can let them know you are interested on Discord. Most of this is crowdsourced, because as a small team, it would be quite a lot of organizing to make it any other way.

I have a cool idea for the game!

: We'd love to hear it, and the best place to share these is on the ⁠suggestions-and-feedback channel on Discord.

Is Not a Cult hiring or looking for help?

: Not a Cult is not usually hiring, but we are always looking for help. Especially translators are appreciated, as the project is 100% community translated. More info on translations can be found on the Localization page here on the wiki. If there is some other area, where you think you could be of special help, you can contact us at contact@walkscape.app If you want to submit an open job application, you can do so at hiring@walkscape.app

Is there a place I can ask a specific question?

: The fastest way to get a question answered right now is through Discord. However asking on Reddit or on the Portal works as well!

Is there somewhere I can look for troubleshooting?

: There is a basic troubleshooting guide on the sidebar of the wiki for help! We always recommend coming to the Discord for particular issues however!

I need support or need to contact the team.

: The best place to contact the team is to email support@walkscape.app. Please give us up to a week after emailing the contact email if we are not in an active invite wave, we are a small team trying to focus on development. Alternatively, contact @maxchill or @sha_dos on the discord. Feel free to ask in the discord if we can help with your issue or if you should contact the email. The Discord is also a good place to ask our helpful community for support on common issues, as the dev team is small and cannot guarantee that emails are answered within the same day. : If you're part of the media or need to contact the team on behalf of other official business, send us an email at contact@walkscape.app.

Gameplay Related

Where can I get Fishing line?

: You can find these for sale at the Frosthook Emporium fishing store in Port Skildar in Jarvonia, sold in quantities of 100 daily for 3 coins each.

Where can I find Maple Trees?

: You can find them in Mangrove Forest of the GDTE, which will require the Jarvonian letter of passage - purchased for 4.5K coins at the Fort of Permafrost (Castle) within the Fort of Permafrost in Jarvonia. You can cut them for maple logs with level 30 Woodcutting.

Why does it take (Very Large Number) of Steps to complete this action?

: Your inventory is probably over-filled (29+/28 slots). If the number in your inventory is displayed in RED, then you will need to either bank the excess items or drop them (losing them forever) so that the number is back under your limit and the amount of steps required is not penalized. Please note that this penalty does not affect travelling.

I just got an item and I can't see it in my inventory?

: Collectibles aren't stored in your inventory. You can see them with your achievements. Click your character icon in the top left -> achievements -> collectibles

How do I get skis?

: You can buy Skis from Frusenholm, the next town over from Kallaheim. : Note: The game screen can be somewhat confusing, seeming to tell you that you need skis when travelling forward from Kallaheim. They are however, not actually required, these are shortcuts that you see marked with red diamonds on the map.

How do I use the Ring of homesickness?

: Abilities can be used from the rightmost tab. Keep the ring in your inventory.

How do I use my saved steps?

: By walking. While you have an activity selected, you will use a step from your step bank for each step you take, allowing you to complete actions at "double speed".

Why can't I buy items/accept jobs?

: You might be looking at the shop through the inspect option through the map. Open it up through the location tab instead. : Note: For jobs you may encounter a bug where you can't accept jobs after teleporting, restarting the game helps.

Why can't I cut trees with Log splitter?

: The Log splitter is not a hatchet. You can equip both a hatchet, and a log splitter simultaneously.

I have +100% Fine Material Finding and still find normal materials?

: +100% fine material find does not give you a 100% chance of finding fine materials, it doubles your chance to find them, from 1/100 to 2/100.

Are +% on equipment additive or multiplicative?

: These are multiplicative. You can see more on how equipment attributes are calculated for each one specifically with examples under the attributes page.

Where can I find better crafting equipment?

: Right now, better equipment is mostly found via chests that can be found by training the main skill involved. (IE: Do crafting activities to find crafting equipment.)

Can I wear 2 of the same rings?

: Yes, you can wear 2 of the same ring with no penalty.

Why is level 50 called early game? Is it not just over halfway to 99?

: WalkScape follows the same leveling formula as RuneScape - level 92 is actually just half of the experience needed to get to level 99. So level 50 in a skill is still actually quite early on for a player and they will have much to do before they get it all the way to level 99.

Faction_Reputation.title: Faction Reputation
Faction_Reputation.html:
Faction Reputation is a measure of your acceptance with each of the major in-game political factions. Currently those include Jarvonia, Trellin, Erdwise, and Syrenthia. Faction Reputation is tightly linked to the Jobs and Job Boards, and provide a lot of rewards for your hard work in the different realms, guilds, and factions around Arenum! In addition to geographical realms, Guilds are also planned to use this system in the future.

The Faction Reputation system enables you to level up your reputation in the different in-game realms. This currently may grant you some Skill Experience, Items, Cosmetic rewards, or even access to some special Shops. In this future this may include expanded access to services, shop discounts, new routes, buildings, and cosmetic titles.

Find_Bird_Nests_(Mechanics).title: Find Bird Nests (Mechanics)
Find_Bird_Nests_(Mechanics).html:
Find Bird Nests Calculation

  1. Most Woodcutting activities have a chance to roll to find bird nests, as well as Rooftop jumping activities.
  2. Find bird nests percentage bonuses from attributes is calculated.
  3. These bonuses are added to the base find bird nests multiplier that you have.
  4. The base chance to find bird nests (.4% or 1/250) is multiplied by the calculated find bird nests multiplier.
  5. The modified find bird nests odds are rolled on a loot table to find Bird Nests.

Note that we can quickly get a value by simply adding the total percent find bird nests to 1 and dividing by 200.

Example with No Find Bird Nests Bonuses

If we want to Cut pine trees with no equipment, and we complete a woodcutting action.

  1. Cutting pine trees is able to give Bird Nests in its loot tables.
  2. We have no equipment, so we have no percent bird nest finding bonus. - Bird nest finding bonus = 0.00
  3. We added our bird nest finding bonus to the base bird nest finding multiplier that you have. - 1.00 bird nest finding multiplier + 0.00 bird nest finding bonus = 1.00 calculated bird nest finding multiplier
  4. We multiply the base bird nest finding chance by the calculated bird nest finding multiplier. - 0.004 × 1.00 = 0.004 modified find bird nests odds
  5. The modified find bird nests odds are rolled on a loot table. - Our 0.004 modified find bird nests odds gives us a 1/250 chance per action completed to receive Bird Nests.

Example with a Find Bird Nests Bonus

If we want to Cut pine trees with a Lumberjack shirt, and we complete a woodcutting action.

  1. Cutting pine trees is able to give Bird Nests in its loot tables.
  2. Our Lumberjack shirt gives a +13.0% to find bird nests - Bird nest finding bonus = 0.13
  3. We added our find bird nests bonus to the base find bird nests multiplier that you have. - 1.00 find bird nests multiplier + 0.13 find bird nests bonus = 1.13 calculated find bird nests multiplier
  4. We multiply the base bird nest finding chance by the calculated find bird nests multiplier. - 0.004 × 1.13 = 0.00452 modified find bird nests odds
  5. The modified find bird nests odds are rolled on a loot table. - Our 0.00452 modified find bird nests odds gives us a 1.13/250 chance per action completed to receive Bird Nests.
