Saved_steps.title: Saved steps
Saved_steps.html:
Saved Steps seen from the Character Screen

Saved Steps (sometimes also referred to as the "Step Bank") are where your physical steps get stored when your character is not currently doing an in-game activity and is idle.


Saved Steps are a limited resource whose max size grows with character level, so it's best to pay attention to how long you can do various skill activities so you do not remain idle for longer than your maximum saved steps allowance, as anything over that will be wasted.


If it is no longer possible to continue your action in-game (e.g. you run out of materials, you reach your destination in-game, etc) and you are still taking steps in real life, this value will increase instead. Once you select a new activity, one step from the step bank will apply to your current activity for each step you take in life. So, if you stored 3000 steps in Saved Steps by being idle in-game, the next 3000 steps in real life will be doubled in-game.


You can see the total amount of Saved Steps you currently have next to the maximum you are allowed at any time from the Character Screen. If you begin an activity, you will also see it below the current activity information.

Second_birthday_letter.title: Second birthday letter
Second_birthday_letter.html:
Second birthday letter
Type:Lore item

The Second birthday letteritem is a lore item.

Lore Entry

Welcome back!

Has it already been another year? These go by quick, I am sure it will be another in no time.

Hopefully you've been making some good progress and improving yourself. You should come on by sometime to give me some firsthand tales of your adventures.

I bet you've gone farther than most merchants have dared to wander at this point. Speaking of merchants, the local ones have come by again trying to buy my hut. They say it would be a great spot for some kind of large scale general store, but I don't plan on going anywhere, you might need a place to rest during your journey!

Well that's enough of an old man's ramblings for now, take care! - Herbert

Seth_Kader.title: Seth Kader
Seth_Kader.html:
Seth Kader
Location:Adventurers' Guild Swampost

A man with a crazied look in his eyes. He gives off a strong aura of confidence, and a hint of insanity. He is the only one brave enough left to man an outpost in the middle of a swamp with the Halfmaw around.

Seth Kader is a character who can be found at Adventurers' Guild Swampost in Halfmaw Hideout in the Grand Duchy of Trellin-Erdwise region.

Quote

  • Snakes? Hate 'em! Get rid of 'em all, especially the darn Halfmaw out there. You might as well prepare yourself with whatever you can here, might not survive out there alone without good gear.

Rumors

  • A hidden cave.
  • I heard that some people are finding their way into the bogs after following some bats. Apparently, this leads them to a secret cave of some sort over there. Probably finds them a different way into the swamp altogether too.
  • Lethal injection.
  • Anti-venom? We'd probably have more options for it if we found some well-kept Halfmaw venom. Most don't go looking for that willingly while Halfmaw tracking. Stupid snake makes plenty of victims as it is.
  • Tabloids?
  • Crazy travelers and halflings always come up with nonsense stories in these swamps. Some even draw pictures and stories about it like a Swampman article I once snagged - was good gator bait while out Alligator hunting in Bog Top.

Skill_Level_(Mechanics).title: Skill Level (Mechanics)
Skill_Level_(Mechanics).html:
Note: This attribute has been removed from all the items that contained it. This page is a placeholder for its return in the future.

Old Information

Calculation to Apply Skill Level

  1. The skill level attribute feeds into the calculation for Work Efficiency.
  2. If we look at that calculation we can see that your skill level gives a +1.25% work efficiency bonus for each level over the level requirement of the skill.
  3. The skill level attribute changes our character's effective skill level and in general grants extra work efficiency.
  4. The rest of the calculation proceeds as normal.

Activity Example with Positive Skill Level Attribute

You want to Cut maple trees with a Woodcutting level of 35 and you have a Forester's flannel shirt.

  1. First lets look at the case where you haven't equipped the Forester's flannel shirt. - You are level 35 and the activity has a requirement of level 30.
    • ((35 Skill Level - 30 Activity Level) × 0.0125) = ((5 Levels over Minimum) × 0.0125) = 0.0625 added level efficiency
    • Cut maple trees has a base work amount of 65. 65 ÷ 1.0625 = 62 steps per activity after rounding.
    • See the page Work Efficiency (Mechanics) for the full calculation.
    • So at Woodcutting level 35 completing the activity cut maple trees would take 62 steps per activity if you had nothing equipped.
  2. Now lets look at the case where you have equipped the Forester's flannel shirt. - You are level 35 and the activity has a requirement of level 30. - The Forester's flannel shirt grants +2 Woodcutting levels.
    • (((35 Skill Level + 2 Skill Levels) - 30 Activity Level) × 0.0125) = ((7 Levels over Minimum) × 0.0125) = 0.0875 added level efficiency
    • Cut maple trees has a base work amount of 65. 65 ÷ 1.0875 = 60 steps per activity after rounding.
    • So at Woodcutting level 35 completing the activity cut maple trees would take 60 steps per activity if you had the Forester's flannel shirt equipped.

Skills.title: Skills
Skills.html:
The skills shown on the character screen with their respective levels for the character being played.

There are currently 12 skills in WalkScape.

All skills in WalkScape are trained through taking steps in the real world. Each step contributes to an action, and completing actions grants experience to the corresponding skill.

Skills start at level 1 and through leveling progression can be leveled up until level 99, where they will only gain experience in the skill but no further levels.

The Total Level represents the sum of all of the current levels a character has.

There is also a Character Level that is a "pure" representation of how much you've walked in total. There are no modifiers that can affect it. This level can affect character unlocks like larger saved step amounts and additional toolbelt slots.

For activities involving two skills, the player is only eligible to earn chests in skills that have actual level requirements.

When performing an activity for a skill, only the primary skill is factored in for the player's equipment bonuses, the "2nd Skill" will also be affected by the equipment attributes based toward the "1st Skill" (IE: +1 Exp will apply to the "2nd Skill" as well).

The Progression Tree of Using Skills to Gather and Transform Materials

Skills

SkillUses
AgilityTravelling across the world and accessing shortcuts.
CarpentryWoodworking for turning logs into planks for crafting.
CookingRecipe based skill that turns raw materials into consumables.
CraftingFor turning transformed materials into final usable crafted items.
FishingCatching fish to use as raw materials, primarily in cooking.
ForagingGathering plants as raw materials for use in crafting and cooking.
HuntingGathering animal resources, primary for tailoring but also some cooking.
MiningMines ore based raw materials for use in smithing.
SmithingTurns ores into bars for use in crafting.
TailoringTaking materials gathered from foraging and hunting to make hand, shirt, and pants gear.
TrinketryTurns gems and trinkets into rings and amulets.
WoodcuttingCuts down trees for their logs as materials for carpentry.

Skill Types

Gathering

These skills involve collecting raw materials endlessly without needing resources of their own.

These skills typically require raw materials for use in recipes to create new materials, consumables, or equipment.

Utility

These skills mainly provide aid toward other actions or have special benefits otherwise.

Smithing.title: Smithing
Smithing.html:
Use blazing forges to smelt ores into metal bars, and hammer them into armour or craft useful tools with them.

The Smithingskill allows you to smelt ores into bars as well as create different types of combat equipment. With higher smithing levels, you'll have access to more ores, be able to create better equipment, and use special skilling equipment that can boost your smithing efficiency. You can also receive Smithing Chests as a rare drop from training this skill.

Activities

The following activities can be done indefinitely without needing materials. Some have equipment requirements or other requirements that need to be satisfied in order to start the activity.

For activities involving two skills, the player is only eligible to earn chests in skills that have actual level requirements.

So, if the activity has a Smithing level requirement, it will be eligible to drop Smithing Chests.

When performing an activity for a skill, only the primary skill is factored in for the player's equipment bonuses, the "2nd Skill" will also be affected by the equipment attributes based toward the "1st Skill" (IE: +1 Exp will apply to the "2nd Skill" as well).

Steps_Required_(Mechanics).title: Steps Required (Mechanics)
Steps_Required_(Mechanics).html:
Calculation to Apply Steps Required

  1. The calculation for Work Efficiency or Travelling Efficiency is applied first.
  2. The calculated number of required steps has the Steps Required attribute value applied. - -X or -X% steps required reduces the amount of steps for the activity. This can decrease the number of steps below the work efficiency cap. - +X or +X% steps required increases the amount of steps for the activity. This can increase the number of step to above it's base value.
  3. The calculated steps are compared to the global minimum of 10. If it is less than 10 then it is set to 10 step per action.
  4. The new required step value is shown after rounding up.

The full formula is:
Steps per action = ceiling(max(((Base Steps ÷ Work Efficiency) × % Steps Required Modifier) + Flat Steps Required Modifier, 10)

Activity Example with a Negative Steps Attribute

If we want to Fry a perch while wearing Oven mittens at Cooking level 30.

  1. Oven mittens give a -2.0 steps required while cooking.
  2. First, we do the Work efficiency calculation to find out the number of steps required with our Cooking levels and Work efficiency. - The base work for frying a perch is 70. - We have a total of 1.3625 cooking efficiency from our cooking levels which reduces the work to 51.376... steps. - We subtract the steps required attribute from the steps per action. 51.376... steps per action - 2.0 steps required = 49.376... steps per action. - We compare to the global minimum of 10 and find we are over so we round up the calculated steps required. ceiling(49.376...) = 50
  3. The final steps required is 50 steps per action to fry a perch with only oven mittens equipped.

Travelling Example with a Negative Steps Attribute Item

If we want to do travel from Barbantok to the Nomad Woods while wearing Medieval sneakers at Agility level 30.

  1. Medieval sneakers give a -5.0 steps required while travelling.
  2. First, we do the Travelling Efficiency calculation to find out the number of steps required with our Agility levels and Work efficiency. - The Base Distance for the Route between Barbantok and the Nomad Woods is 342 steps. - We have a total of 1.30 travelling efficiency which reduces the distance to 270 after rounding giving 27 steps per section of the distance. - We subtract the steps required attribute from the steps per action. 27 steps per action - 5.0 steps required = 25 steps per action.
  3. The final steps required is 25 steps per action between Barbantok and the Nomad Wood for a total travelling distance of 250 steps.

Travelling Example with a Positive Steps Attribute Item

If we want to do travel from Barbantok to the Nomad Woods while wearing Traveler's kit at Agility level 30.

  1. The Traveler's kit gives a +10.0 steps required while travelling.
  2. First, we do the Travelling Efficiency calculation to find out the number of steps required with our Agility levels and Work efficiency. - The Base Distance for the Route between Barbantok and the Nomad Woods is 342 steps. - We have a total of 1.30 travelling efficiency which reduces the distance to 270 after rounding giving 27 steps per section of the distance. - We add the steps required attribute from the steps per action. 27 steps per action + 10.0 steps required = 37 steps per action.
  3. The final steps required is 37 steps per action between Barbantok and the Nomad Wood for a total travelling distance of 370 steps.

Activity Example with Negative Percent and Base Steps Attribute

If we want to do Rescue team while using a Good Wanderlust walking stick and Flowing pocketwatch at Agility level 30.

  1. Good Wanderlust walking stick gives a -2 steps required while Agility.
  2. Flowing pocketwatch gives a global -5% steps required.
  3. First, we do the Work efficiency calculation to find out the number of steps required with our Agility levels and Work efficiency. - The base work for Rescue team is 8500. - We have a total of 1.0 Agility efficiency from our Agility levels and 0.05 from the Good Wanderlust walking stick which reduces the work to 8095.238... (no rounding yet). - We multiply by the percent step reduction first before the flat reduction. 8095.238... × (100% base - 0.05% steps required) = 7690.476... steps per action - We subtract the steps required attribute from the steps per action. 7690.476... steps per action - 2.0 steps required = 7688.476... steps per action. - We compare to the global minimum of 10 and find we are over so we round up the calculated steps required. ceiling(7688.476...) = 7689
  4. The final steps required is 7689 steps per action for Rescue team with both sources of minus steps.

Syrenthia.title: Syrenthia
Syrenthia.html:
Syrenthia is a mini-realm located in the sea between Jarvonia and GDTE. This underwater realm is centered around the city of Vastalume is home to the Syrenthians a diverse people led by Kalmar The Neverdrowning.

To access this region, players will need to acquire a 3 pieces of the Diving Gear Set.

  • Darktide Trench
  • Elara's Lagoon
  • Kelp Forest
  • Underwater Cave

Factions

Syrenthia

The Syrenthia faction composes the entire underwater realm. Jobs done for the Syrenthia faction will reward you with Syrenthia Faction Reputation and advance the Syrenthia faction reward track.

System_Requirements.title: System Requirements
System_Requirements.html:
Minimum requirements:

Android

  • Android version 10+ required.
  • Google Play Services
  • Health Connect (Optional, for wearable support other than Samsung)
  • Part of Android in version 14+, installed from the play store in versions 10-13.

iOS

  • iOS version 13+ required
  • Apple Health (optional, only for wearable support)

Supported smart watch and wearable devices

Since April 2025, WalkScape supports loading steps from wearable devices, such as smart watches and smart rings when playing on iOS, and for Android from version +452 in September 2025. Not every single device is or will be supported. It's important to note that while in the testing phase of the feature we are more lax about step sources, but might at some point restrict the feature only to those platforms that work reliably enough.

WalkScape doesn't sync steps straight from the device or from vendor-specific apps, but instead uses Apple Health, Google Health Connect or the Samsung Health API as standardized storages for step information. In general, any device that can sync to these services should be usable with WalkScape. Usually this involves a secondary application that gets the steps from the device, then syncs them to Apple Health or Health Connect. An example of such is Garmin Connect for the Garmin ecosystem. These applications have several differences between them and some work better than others. A few work so poorly, that they have had to be disabled all together from counting as step sources.

Below is a table of different step sources, where we know from testing or feedback how well they perform. If the app or source you are using is not listed below, then it means that it most likely works (as long as it can be synced to Apple Health/Health Connect), but cannot be guaranteed to work. Most sources are not listed, since we just haven't had enough experience with that specific brand. If a vendor is supported, then it's fairly safe to say that their devices work with the game and if a source is listed as not supported, then it won't work.

If your wearable device does not work with WalkScape on Android, you can try out Health Sync app that supports some less popular wearables.

Tailoring.title: Tailoring
Tailoring.html:
Enter the loom with a needle, thread, and fabric to create clothes for all sorts of environments.

The Tailoringskill allows you to create hand, chest and leg gear. Some tailoring tasks are simple (like making Linen cloth) while others are more complex, requiring many materials. With higher tailoring levels, you'll have access to more materials from foraging and hunting to use to make your gear, better recipes, and special skilling equipment that can boost your tailoring efficiency. You can also receive Tailoring chests as a rare drop from training this skill.

Activities

The following activities can be done indefinitely without needing materials. Some have equipment requirements or other requirements that need to be satisfied in order to start the activity.

For activities involving two skills, the player is only eligible to earn chests in skills that have actual level requirements.

So, if the activity has a Tailoring level requirement, it will be eligible to drop Tailoring Chests.

When performing an activity for a skill, only the primary skill is factored in for the player's equipment bonuses, the "2nd Skill" will also be affected by the equipment attributes based toward the "1st Skill" (IE: +1 Exp will apply to the "2nd Skill" as well).

Tips.title: Tips
Tips.html:
Tips are messages to help explain of give information about game mechanics.

Tips

  • Being overencumbered only slows down your activities, but doesn't affect travel.
  • The base chance to find FINE materials is 1/100, which you can increase with better gear and tools.
  • The base chance to find most Chests is 1/250, which you can increase with better gear and tools.
  • Attributes involving a percent symbol % are multiplicative (For Example: +10% Fine material finding gives 1.1/100).
  • Long pressing an item opens multi-selection options in the inventory.
  • The tongs button at the bottom of the screen opens the crafting interface.
  • Pressing the mini-map at the top-right opens the full map for travel options.
  • You can find achievements and obtained collectible items by tapping your character at the top-left.
  • Collectibles you find give 1 extra achievement point per item!
  • Many NPCs can tell you rumours to help find things in the game.
  • The hamburger menu at the bottom-right (or bottom-left in left handed mode) has your WalkPedia to help track your total progress.
  • Pay attention to the specifics of an achievement - some only count toward the unlock if a drop comes from an activity directly.
  • Make sure you equip your items to get their effects, most don't work from inventory alone.
  • Bank space is unlimited, if you are worried about the usage of something, bank it!
  • If there's maintenance, don't worry, usually your steps will still count during the downtime. Check the Discord announcements to be sure!
  • Check out our Portal, Reddit, and Discord for announcements, updates, and development blogs.
  • Found something broken or have a suggestion? Report it to us on Discord! Your reports help improve the game!
  • Quality outcome will help raise the chances for better quality items seen at the bottom of recipes in the crafting interface.
  • Skill levels exceeding an activity's main skill requirement gives +1.25% extra Work efficiency for what you're doing, up to 20 levels.
  • Skill levels exceeding a recipe's main skill requirement in the crafting interface provide additional Quality outcome.
  • Equipping a gear set while at a bank will automatically withdraw all the items from the bank.
  • Hunting activities that require inputs get bonuses from using FINE versions of them! Check the interface for what they give!
  • Want to find something particular about the game and don't mind spoilers? Check the Wiki!
  • Enjoying the game? It is thanks to all our supporters that have done so on Patreon and Buy Me A Coffee!
  • Hunting activities that require inputs give twice the rolls of their main loot table!

Toolbelt.title: Toolbelt
Toolbelt.html:
The toolbelt interface.

The Tools tab shows all the tools that the player is wielding on their toolbelt. The toolbelt serves a few purposes in WalkScape. Firstly, it simplifies inventory management by keeping tools neatly organized and separate from your main inventory bag, preventing clutter. Additionally, it ensures you won't accidentally leave your tools behind in your bank or elsewhere, as they'll always be conveniently stored in your toolbelt.

Tools function quite similarly to gear, but instead of having one slot for each type of gear (like helmets, pants, or shoes), your toolbelt can accommodate any item that serves as a tool. The only limitation is that you can't equip two of the same type of tool for the same skill—no fishing with two fishing rods! This restriction helps to avoid creating overpowered combos, as all buffs gained from tools in the toolbelt are active. Items stored in your toolbelt won't take up space in your inventory bag.

When you start the game, you'll have only three slots for tools. As you progress, you can unlock three more slots by increasing your Character Level to levels 20, 50, and 80.

Most skills will require you to have a particular type of tool on your toolbelt. For example, you can't engage in woodcutting if you don't have an axe in your toolbelt. While tools make your work much more efficient, they're also essential for performing certain activities in the game.

Travelling_(Mechanics).title: Travelling (Mechanics)
Travelling_(Mechanics).html:
Travelling is a basic game activity that uses the Agility skill in a way that is unique and different from other activities. This can be noticed in how the game calculates experience, how chest drops are handled, and how it applies efficiency.

Travelling Experience Formula

Experience = Base Distance * (0.096736) × 2.718280.016592 × Agility level

Note that the formula does not take your travelling efficiency into account - which can be obtained from you Agility level as well.

The Base Distance is the raw distance between two locations that form a Route - without modifiers.

A list of all routes can be found here.

Travelling Chest Chance

An Agility chest has a chance to drop whenever a travelling action is completed. Each route is divided into 10 actions, and each action makes an independent chest roll.

The base chest chance is calculated using the route's Base Steps shown on the Routes page. Player Agility level, work efficiency, and steps required modifiers change the number of steps needed to complete the route, but do not change this base chest chance.

Chest Chance per Action (%) = max(0.1, Base Steps ÷ 2,510.04)

The minimum base chance is 0.1% per action. This minimum applies to routes with 251 base steps or less.

The chance of finding at least one chest during a full route can be calculated as:

Chance per Route = 1 − (1 − Chest Chance per Action)10

For this formula, the chance per action must be written as a decimal. For example, 0.335% is written as 0.00335.

Example for the Route from Kallaheim to Frusenholm

The route from Kallaheim to Frusenholm is 840 Base Steps.

  1. Calculate the chest chance for one travelling action: - 840 ÷ 2510.04 = 0.334656% - This is bigger than 0.1% so we use it directly.
  2. Convert the chance into approximate odds: - 1 ÷ 0.00334656 = 298.81 - This is approximately 1 in 299 travelling actions.
  3. Calculate the chance of finding at least one chest during all 10 actions: - 1 − (1 − 0.00334656)10 = 0.032966 - This is approximately a 3.30% chance per completed route, or about 1 in 30 routes.

These are base chances before any Chest finding attributes are applied.

Travelling Efficiency Calculation

  1. Each set of points has an initial base distance between them, described as work, with 1 work unit equating to 1 step.
  2. This base then has efficiencies applied to it. The efficiencies are obtained from leveling up agility and from equipment bonuses. Agility gives a +0.5% efficiency bonus for each level when travelling. The equipment bonus is as stated in the details for that item for either Agility or Travelling. These bonuses are added to the base 100% efficiency that you have for every activity. The new distance is the base distance divided by the efficiency (as a number, not a percent).
  3. This calculated distance is then divided by 10 to create the individual action between each location.
  4. The steps per action are then modified by any direct step reduction from items. - Minimum of 10 steps per action
  5. The steps per action are then rounded up to the nearest full step.
  6. Finally, the calculated steps are multiplied by 10 to get the displayed distance between locations.

Note: There is no work efficiency cap on travelling.

Example with Agility levels Only

If we want to travel from the Disenchanted Forest to Kallaheim with an agility level of 30 and no gear.

  1. We want to travel from the Disenchanted Forest to Kallaheim. - There is a base distance of 450 work units (steps).
  2. We have level 30 agility, so we need to calculate the efficiency from levels. - 450 steps ÷ (1.00 base efficiency + (30 × 0.005 level efficiency)) = 450 steps ÷ (1.00 base efficiency + 0.15 total level efficiency) = 450 steps ÷ 1.15 total efficiency = 391.30 steps with efficiency
  3. We take the calculated 391.30 steps between Disenchanted Forest to Kallaheim and divide by 10. - 391.30 steps ÷ 10 actions = 39.130 steps per action
  4. We have no step reduction so the steps per action remains the same. - 39.130 steps per action - 0.0 steps per action = 39.130 corrected steps per action
  5. We need to round the corrected steps per action. - 39.130 corrected steps per action rounds up to 40 steps per action
  6. We calculate the new total distance to display. - 40 rounded steps per action × 10 actions = 400 displayed steps between the Disenchanted Forest and Kallaheim

Example with Agility levels and Work Efficiency Gear

If we want to travel from the Disenchanted Forest to Kallaheim with an agility level of 30 and a Walking stick which has a +5.0% work efficiency for agility.

  1. We want to travel from the Disenchanted Forest to Kallaheim. - There is a base distance of 450 work units (steps).
  2. We have level 30 agility, and +5.0% from our gear so we need to calculate the efficiency from both. - 450 steps ÷ (1.00 base efficiency + (30 × 0.005 level efficiency) + 0.05 item efficiency) = 450 steps ÷ (1.00 base efficiency + 0.15 total level efficiency + 0.05 item efficiency) = 450 steps ÷ 1.20 total efficiency = 375.00 steps with efficiency
  3. We take the calculated 375.00 steps between Disenchanted Forest to Kallaheim and divide by 10. - 375.00 steps ÷ 10 actions = 37.500 steps per action.
  4. We have no step reduction so the steps per action remains the same. - 37.500 steps per action - 0.0 steps per action = 37.500 corrected steps per action
  5. We need to round the corrected steps per action. - 37.500 corrected steps per action rounds up to 38 steps per action
  6. We calculate the new total distance to display. - 38 rounded steps per action × 10 actions = 380 displayed steps between the Disenchanted Forest and Kallaheim

Example with Agility levels, Work Efficiency Gear, and Step Reduction Gear

If we want to travel from the Disenchanted Forest to Kallaheim with an agility level of 30 and Medieval sneakers which have a +15.0% work efficiency for travelling, and a flat -5.0 steps required for travelling.

  1. We want to travel from the Disenchanted Forest to Kallaheim. - There is a base distance of 450 work units (steps).
  2. We have level 30 agility, and +5.0% from our gear so we need to calculate the efficiency from both. - 450 steps ÷ (1.00 base efficiency + (25 × 0.005 level efficiency) + 0.15 item efficiency) = 450 steps ÷ (1.00 base efficiency + 0.15 total level efficiency + 0.15 item efficiency) = 450 steps ÷ 1.30 total efficiency = 346.15 steps with efficiency
  3. We take the calculated 346.15 steps between Disenchanted Forest to Kallaheim and divide by 10. - 346.15 steps ÷ 10 actions = 34.615 steps per action.
  4. We have a -5.0 step reduction from our gear so we need to reduce the steps per action. - 34.615 steps per action - 5.0 steps per action = 29.615 corrected steps per action
  5. We need to round the corrected steps per action. - 29.615 corrected steps per action rounds up to 30 steps per action
  6. We calculate the new total distance to display. - 30 rounded steps per action × 10 actions = 300 displayed steps between the Disenchanted Forest and Kallaheim.

Trinketry.title: Trinketry
Trinketry.html:
The art of gemistry, gemology and jewelcrafting - the creation of beautiful and valuable items from precious stones.

The Trinketryskill allows you to shape rough gems into cut gems as well as create rings and amulets. With higher Trinketry levels, you'll have access to more recipes, be able to create better equipment, and use special skilling equipment that can boost your Trinketry efficiency. You can also receive Trinketry chests as a rare drop from training this skill.

Activities

The following activities can be done indefinitely without needing materials. Some have equipment requirements or other requirements that need to be satisfied in order to start the activity.

For activities involving two skills, the player is only eligible to earn chests in skills that have actual level requirements.

So, if the activity has a Trinketry level requirement, it will be eligible to drop Trinketry Chests.

When performing an activity for a skill, only the primary skill is factored in for the player's equipment bonuses, the "2nd Skill" will also be affected by the equipment attributes based toward the "1st Skill" (IE: +1 Exp will apply to the "2nd Skill" as well).

Recipes

The following activities are completed through recipes and thus require materials. Additionally, they may have service requirements, usually in the form of a service location. All recipes produce one of the final products by default.

Tutorial.title: Tutorial
Tutorial.html:
Below is the Tutorial as you will find it in-game. Some UI elements may change as improvements are ongoing and the tutorial will be improved as the game develops.

When starting the game and before being shown the tutorial, you will enter character creation where you will first choose your starting region (currently has no impact, so it is just flavor text), race (only humans currently available), and appearance (all of these are visual with no in-game impacts).

Welcome to WalkScape!

I'm very happy to see you join WalkScape's Closed Beta.


As you may know, the game is still under development, and the game you see here is only the core of the game.

The game is still very limited in terms of features and content, and we are expanding the game continuously throughout the beta.

There might also be issues: bugs, exploits and unbalanced content found in the game. Some of these might result in needing to either roll back or restart the server - both of which we want to avoid as much as possible, but important to keep in mind that they're a possibility.

With all of that out of the way, thank you for joining us, and helping to test the game. You can continue this tutorial by either pressing “NEXT” at the bottom of the page, or pressing “QUIT” to quit the tutorial. I highly recommend to play through the tutorial, as the game is quite different.

Basic navigation

The basic navigation of the game might be slightly different from typical applications and games, especially for iOS users. Here are some good things to remember:

Some game views have no back buttons such as crafting and inventory. You can navigate back from views by doing a "back swipe" by swiping the edge of either left or right side of the screen.

Most of the game views, including the main view and inventory, are also navigateable by swiping left or right between the different tabs.

The “hamburger button” at the main view bottom right corner opens up options to navigate to different menus, such as leaderboard.

Your character's profile picture at the top left corner can be pressed, and opens your character information.

The inventory counter, green crafting symbol and minimap can be pressed to open inventory, crafting or world map respectively. World map is used for travelling.

You can open more game menu options by pressing the “hamburger button” at the main game view.

Activities and actions

The core of the game is that you select an activity for your character, and complete actions by walking in real life. Each activity takes a certain number of steps to complete an action. The number of steps needed can be brought down via gear and items.

You can see information about your current location by swiping left. From world map, you can find information about other locations that you've previously visited by tapping locations and swiping right.

Gathering activities are unlimited - they repeat infinitely. Crafting and Travelling activities are limited, meaning that when you arrive at your destination or run out of crafting materials, the activity ends.

If you walk while your character has no activity selected, your steps will go towards “Saved Steps”. Saved steps are consumed on future activities, so you practically can never waste steps in WalkScape.

If you change your activity, the current activity ends. Any steps that were already contributed towards the current action will be refunded to your “Saved Steps”.

Begin your journey

Those are the basics of the game! You'll see these tutorial messages pop up while you interact with new things in the game, if you decide not to skip the tutorial.

As your first thing, you should swipe left to the Location page, and scroll down to Visit Helpful Herbert's Hut. Press the Help-option there, and he will give you a gift to help you get started in WalkScape.

I hope you enjoy the game! We also have a Wiki for WalkScape with a new player guide.

Selecting activities

Selecting activities for your character to complete is the most important way for progressing in the game. Activities reward you with items and experience when you complete “actions”.

You can find the activities below the location image. On smaller screens, you might need to scroll slightly to find the activities listed. The activity listing shows buttons for different skills that have possible activities available at the location. The number below the button indicates how many options are available.

Opening and starting activities can be done in the location view and alternatively in activity view if you have no current activity selected.

Visiting buildings

Another important thing that you can do in some locations is visiting buildings. Not every location has buildings.

The most important buildings are definitely shops and banks. You can use NPC shops for buying and selling your items. Banks are useful when you want to store items for later use. You can quickly deposit items from your inventory if your location has a bank when long tapping an item and choosing the option from bottom right.

While in Disenchanted Forest, the starting location, you should Visit Helpful Herbert's Hut. He will give you some items to get you started.

Some locations have buildings that you can visit.

Using services

Some locations - especially cities and towns - also have services. You need services in order to craft certain items. Here are the most commonly needed services during early game:

Forges. Forges are necessary when you want to do smithing, like smelting bars or creating armor. You can find the nearest forge in Kallaheim.

Sawmills. Sawmills are necessary when you want to do carpentry, like creating planks out of logs. You can find the nearest sawmill in Kallaheim.

Kitchens. Kitchens are necessary when you want to do cooking, like creating consumables that give temporary buffs. You can find the nearest kitchen in Kallaheim.

Workshops. Workshops are necessary when you want to do crafting, like creating tools such as pickaxes and fishing rods. You can find the nearest workshop in Frusenholm, east of Kallaheim. Basic tools have no service requirements.

Visiting Helpful Herbert's Hut

As your first thing, you should pay a visit to Herbert. He's located in Disenchanted Forest, and helps you to get started in the game.

Visit Herbert by scrolling down the location view the location view in Disenchanted Forest and pressing “Visit”.

Choose a starting skill

Well now, Newbie! There's a lot you can do around here. I can give you something to get you started. What would you be interested in?

Getting started

I also have some sticks and stones gathered here if you want to make some basic tools yourself. Check them out if you like to make more tools.

You can get free stones and sticks from Herbert by pressing “Buy items” button while visiting his hut. If you want to build other tools, this is a useful option. You can long press the “+ button” to select all while in shops or banks.


Woodcutting is essential skill for building things: many tools require planks, which can only be made out of logs. Woodcutting is important for Carpentry.

Starting Location: You can start woodcutting here in Disenchanted Forest.

Where to find: Forest locations usually contain woodcuttingactivities.

Used for: Gaining logs, which are useful for carpentry.


Mining is essential skill for making things out of metal: armor, weapons and tools require metals, which can be gained from mining ores. Mining is important for smithing.

Starting Location: You can start mining in Pit of Pittance, west from Disenchanted Forest.

Where to find: Mountain and hill locations usually contain miningactivities.

Used for: Gaining ores, which are useful for smithing.


Foraging is essential skill for finding plants: plants are used in many skills. This makes foraging great for a lot of things, like crafting and cooking.

Starting Location:: You can start foraging here in Disenchanted Forest.

Where to find: All nature locations (plains, forests, hills, mountains, beaches) can contain foragingactivities.

Used for: Gaining plants, which are useful for many skills


Fishing is essential skill for catching raw fish: fish can be cooked, and even some more complex cooking recipes use fish. Fishing is important for cooking.

Starting Location: You can start fishing in Beach of Woes, west from Disenchanted Forest.

Where to find: Water locations (beaches, coasts, lakes, rivers) usually contain fishingactivities.

Used for: Gaining fish, which are useful for cooking.

Versions/571.title: Version 571
Versions/571.html:
+571 QoL & OTA Update

Added

  • OTA system added for game data and localizations
  • Ability rework, including: new UIs, Ability charges, Activity abilities, and more
  • While you were away displays your used saved steps
  • You can now select the amount of actions you want to complete an activity for
  • Skills are now categorized into Gathering, Artisan and Utility
  • Updated to Flutter 3.38.3, which should improve stability & performance
  • Updated to new Health Connect client v. 1.1.0, which should fix issues with Garmin and others
  • Added reordering to Gear Sets
  • Added sorting button to Inventory
  • Added deposit all button to Inventory
  • Added quick ways to rename gearsets in Gear Set manager
  • Added a Work Efficiency breakdown to Activity page
  • Consumable cards have been reworked to be more clean looking and dense, same with Inventory Full and Saved Steps
  • Gear Set management and selection pages have been combined together
  • Tab bars (inventory, crafting, leaderboards, achievements/profile page) have been reworked to be more clean looking and performant
  • WalkPedia quick button (the skill icon right of your profile picture) now takes you to the output item page in WalkPedia while crafting
  • Toggle to disable Agility XP added as a temporary way for people to do challenge characters
  • You can now withdraw a gear set from bank without equipping it
  • Item abilities can now be used straight from inventory view
  • Added a button to hide the overlays in the world map, so you can admire the world map better
  • Game version added to the character data exports for 3rd party developers
  • New translations from community translators
  • You can now browse Tips of the Day
  • Activity sprite visible in Activity View
  • Tooltip widget added, and some tooltips added where text isn't necessary to show all the time under these tooltips
  • A restart game button added once your client has downloaded an OTA update during a gameplay session

Changed

  • All in-game fonts have been changed to support Slavic languages and more
  • AI generated art assets removed from the game where isometric art pieces have already replaced them, bringing down the application size significantly
  • Crafting Outcome has been renamed to Quality Outcome
  • Basic tools have been split from Copper by making Copper tools require level 2
  • Changes:
    • Spin Flax into Twine - Service Requirement Removed, also renamed from "Spin Flax into Rope"
    • Weave a Basic Fishing Net - Moved from lvl 1 to 2
    • Craft a Copper Hatchet - Moved from lvl 1 to 2
    • Craft a Copper Pickaxe - Moved from lvl 1 to 2
    • Make a Copper Sickle - Moved from lvl 1 to 2
    • Craft Kelp Twine - Renamed from "Craft Kelp Rope"
  • Changed "Level up XYZ times" to "Have a total level of XYZ"
  • Affects Alien squeaky toy
  • WalkPedia max work efficiency now uses the same kind of display style as the new activity view WE breakdown

Fixed

  • Optimizations to Bank
  • Optimizations to Gear Sets
  • General optimizations across the application to improve performance
  • Optimizations to Travelling
  • Locations unlocked from rumors are now correctly displayed in WalkPedia (until you've visited them)
  • Fixed the small "bubble" notifications in game, they shouldn't get stuck anymore and should work smoother
  • Content that is only meant for development versions of the game are now removed from production builds. WalkPedia totals should now be possible to complete fully
  • WalkPedia remembers your opened categories so they stay opened when you go back to previous views
  • WalkPedia lists are ordered alphabetically
  • Pressing the minus button on sliders when at minimum value now flips it to the max value
  • Fixed the Turkish i-character when capitalized
  • Fixed Gear Sets page not updating properly when doing changes to Gear Sets
  • UI fixes to overflowing texts, spacings and font sizes
  • Fixes to deleting characters
  • Fixes to updating the PFP image
  • Eye accessory toggle now works in the character creation UI
  • Fixed searching for PFP options in shops
  • Faction reputation numbers now round down on the X/Z counter widgets
  • Fixes to PFP rendering where layers were wrongly ordered for image exports/server side PFPs
  • Fix to iOS and Android crash issue when using smart watch activity recording
  • A lot of small bug fixes across the game!

Undocumented

  • Kallaheim Isometric Image
  • Casbrant Fields Isometric Image
  • Azurazera Isometric Image
  • Winter's End Isometric Image
  • Adventuring fishing pole icon
  • Butterfly catching icon

Versions/645.title: Version 645
Versions/645.html:
+645 Hunting & Tailoring Map Update

Added

  • Overhauled world map featuring: Location search, visibility settings and seeing your friends!
  • Many small improvements and fixes
  • Added a new button to gear sets: Import and Equip. It does not add a new gear set but only equips the set you have in your clipboard
  • Added counts in crafting view to materials
  • (Keywords) 1 new keyword
  • Upgradeable Keyword
  • (Loot Tables) 2 new loot tables
  • Gecko egg in Lizard hunting and Mine coal
  • (Items) 1 new item
  • Gecko egg
  • (Pets) 1 new pet
  • Gecko
  • (Locations) ISO art added for Salsfirth, Granfiddich, Witched Woods

Fixed

  • Collectible sorting should be fixed (again)
  • Bank deposit now uses clamping, so depositing a larger amount than available should still deposit everything successfully
  • Fixed that DA and DR notifications appeared after location arrival notifications
  • Collectible drops should again update the count properly
  • Saved character image file had no name
  • Fixed that abilities with steps cooldown are only ticked down on action completion
  • Fixed gear set search not updating when not selecting a skill
  • Fixed duplicate crafting errors in Crafting Bottom Sheet
  • Fixed the issue with Sail Repair where fabric optionality did not work properly
  • Fixed chest drops being counted twice for WalkPedia
  • Fixed the WalkPedia pages counting chest and activity source gains incorrectly
  • Fixed wrapping for ability input requirement texts
  • Fixed pet name font size in attribute listing
  • Fixed that activities did not cancel if you used queue to equip a gear set but did not have the correct item actually equipped
  • Fixed opening multiple instances of WalkPedia
  • (PFP Options) Added missing layer for Mummy Outfit so that it displays over the player's face
  • (Recipes) Fixed Tarsilium arrows recipe to appropriately require Teak logs instead of Willow logs

Changed

  • Changed the 'failed to verify' message
  • Fixed the screwdriver issue in All attributes listing
  • Back gestures exit the world map
  • (Activities) The desert mining activities no longer require the Navigate Desert ability to do them
  • (Activities) 2 different activities had a new loot table added to them
  • Gecko egg in Lizard hunting and Mine coal
  • (Items) Birch hunting bow WE halved while CF doubled on all rarities

Versions/647.title: Version 647
Versions/647.html:
+645 Hunting & Tailoring Map Update #2

Changed

  • World Map: Standardised zoom level for Double Tap, Initial Zoom, Focus
  • World Map: Made most map animations smoother due to some users complaining about motion sickness (will be a setting and further tweaked in the future)
  • World Map: Removed location search functionality temporarily as it's a bit too unstable — Proper fix coming soon
  • World Map: Tapping the map will stop any inertia (for all you fast swipers out there that need an emergency break)

Fixed

  • World Map: Fixed 'Hide All' visibility toggle

Versions/657.title: Version 657
Versions/657.html:
+655 Hunting & Tailoring QoL Update

Added

  • Removed all of the remaining AI assets from the game, reducing the application size by 31mb
  • Collectibles now show up as the first items under action completed and have special styling
  • You can now deposit only some items from a selected inventory slot
  • Added a loading spinner to WalkPedia and made it open the page faster
  • (World Map) Added more realms
  • (Keywords) 2 new keywords and 2 new search keywords (one is "weight medium" keyword which stacks at 100)
  • Medium Weight
  • Snowy Location
  • (Locations) ISO art added for Halfling Campgrounds, Halfmaw Hideout, Bog Bottom, Bog Top, Old Arena Ruins, Red Coast and Bilgemont Port

Changed

  • (World Map) Re-enabled location search (we fixed it :D)
  • (World Map) Made location icons visible from further away
  • Double action no longer uses consumables on the extra action
  • Gear set equipping behavior changed - empty slots are now not unequipped. Instead the character keeps whatever is already equipped in a slot if you are equipping a set with empty slots
  • When withdrawing gear sets from bank, the withdraw option no longer withdraws items that you already have in your inventory
  • Withdrawing gear sets also checks for items you have equipped and does not withdraw items that you have already equipped
  • Import & equip button now also closes the gear set page
  • Ordering of gear changed in gear sets to follow the same order as gear view uses
  • (Locations) Blackspell Harbour renamed to Blackspell Harbour and icon updated
  • (Keywords) "Light" and "Ultra Light" keywords changed to stack at 1000 and 10 000
  • (Locations) Noiseless Pass has been taken over by Trellin for the GDTE - rejoice
  • (Locations) "Snowy" location keyword applied to Disenchanted Forest, Azurazera, Kallaheim, Frusenholm, Barbantok, Centaham, Port Skildar, Coldington, Sanguine Hills, Nomad Woods, Casbrant Fields, Norsack Plains, Frostbite Mountain, Noiseless Pass, Fort of Permafrost, Beach of Woes, Winter Waves Glacier, Horn of Respite, Black Eye Peak, Winter's End, Nurturing Nook Springs, and Pit of Pittance
  • (Items) Birch skis keywords for regional and Jarvonia search removed in place of snowy search
  • (Items) Birch skis attributes for while in Jarvonia realm changed to while in a snowy location
  • (Items) Pine skis keywords for regional and Jarvonia search removed in place of snowy search
  • (Items) Pine skis attributes for while in Jarvonia realm changed to while in a snowy location
  • (Items) Oak skis keywords for regional and Jarvonia search removed in place of snowy search
  • (Items) Oak skis attributes for while in Jarvonia realm changed to while in a snowy location
  • (Items) Bert's super-skis keywords for regional and Jarvonia search removed in place of snowy search
  • (Items) Bert's super-skis attributes for while in Jarvonia realm changed to while in a snowy location
  • (Items) Ectoplasm scraps now have hide and medium weight keywords
  • (Pets) Changed camel to use location keywords for "desert" for XP/attribute requirements in place of "Wrentmark"
  • (Pets) Changed reindeer to use location keywords for "snowy" for XP/attribute requirements in place of "Jarvonia"

Fixed

  • (World Map) Moving camera to locations/player no longer overshoots if triggered while inertia is present
  • (World Map) Realm borders (last zoom level) were redone to work on all devices
  • (World Map) All realms now have icons
  • (World Map) Improved Bottom Sheet behaviour
  • Fixed overflow issues with tags inside text
  • Fixed being able to do bank deposits from any location
  • Deposit button is now only shown when at a bank location & the item can be banked
  • Fixed that using abilities from item view closed the bottom sheet
  • Fixed the this gear set no longer exists error when equipping imported set
  • Withdrawing gear sets now takes quality into account. It withdraws if a higher quality than current in inventory is found, but does not if same quality or lower is found
  • Fixed using phone navigation not dismissing the world map when you have a bottom sheet opened
  • Fixed that GDTE was not wrapping to 2 lines on location info view
  • Fixed the validation error when doing travel + 1 with a summoned pet change
  • Fixed that you could only do one transaction when buying PFP options and needed to re-enter the shop to buy more
  • Player Icon not being centered in away screen
  • Fixed the problem with pet summons when traveling to Kildome cross
  • Now instead of showing 1 000 M steps when not being able to travel, steps until arrival shows N/A
  • Import & Equip now checks if the item is already equipped, and skips if that is the case
  • Fixed getting the same error message twice on incorrect travel pathing
  • Fixed that changing to correct requirement when seeing queued action having invalid requirement now updates the validation
  • Fixed that having incorrect requirements for an traveling activity did not cancel the action
  • Fixed the stack overflow issue happening when summoning pets to queue
  • Fixed the incorrect locale link for WalkPedia loading
  • (PFP Options) Fix mummy outfit not hiding headwear

Versions/660.title: Version 660
Versions/660.html:
+660 Hunting & Tailoring Bugfix Update

Changed

  • Made world map camera movement more responsive, supports multiple touch panning
  • Made camera behave like world map

Fixed

  • Fixed gear sets not being able to equip two of the same rings
  • Fixed that Use button for consumables did not work
  • Fixed the weirdness in Items in Use warnings
  • Fixed that withdrawing gear set withdraws 2 rings if two of the same rings are in the gear set
  • Using abilities now collapse the entire sheet stack
  • Equipping gear sets now equips items in other sets if they are in different slots and retains the correct tools slots
  • Fixed the problem when equipping sets with items that have the same banned keywords
  • Fixed the count in multiple material requirements while crafting using the first value for all subsequent options
  • Activity sheet page data is now emptied when reopened, meaning that complete until actions no longer persists when switching between activities
  • Fixed double while you were away screens when foregrounding the game when there was one already opened

Unannounced

  • (Locations) ISO art added for Blackspell Harbour
Versions/660.text: +660 Hunting & Tailoring Bugfix Update Changed Made world map camera movement more responsive, supports multiple touch panning Made camera behave like world map Fixed Fixed gear sets not being able to equip two of the same rings Fixed that Use button for consumables did not work

Versions/666.title: Version 666
Versions/666.html:
+666 Release of the Beast Update

Added

  • Added a new feature: Mailbox
  • Added a new service type: Mailbox. Mailboxes are available in each location with a bank (as long as you have the bank unlocked)
  • Added a Mail button to inventory so you can open the mailbox from there as well
  • Now if processing a button takes a while, it will turn into a loading spinner
  • Added while away and bubble notifications for gaining PFP options
  • Added a button to location routes to make it easier to navigate to routes from existing locations (including unknowns)
  • Smooth slider applied to everywhere.
  • Sliders now have divisions when the max count is less than 10
  • Pets are now reorderable
  • Pet eggs are now reorderable
  • Active pet or egg is now shown on the bottom sheet for choosing eggs/pets. You can also press it to open up the Pet/Egg page.
  • Can't sell locked items from inventory to Mysterious Merchant. You're shown a warning if you're selling favorited items.
  • Added Lore items type
  • Added Lore items page (found next to where you open the Collectibles listing)
  • Collectibles and Lore Items pages now use the new title style
  • (Items) 6 new items
  • Pixie egg
  • Adventurers' guild buckler
  • Collection ring
  • Treasure hunter bandolier

Versions/679.title: Version 679
Versions/679.html:
+679 The 6️⃣7️⃣ Update Bank Rework Patch #1

Added

  • (Bank Rework) Added hunting products & curiosity keywords to hunting-related items
  • (Bank Rework) New default bank category for curiosities
  • (Bank Rework) You can now see how much of something you are withdrawing
  • (Bank Rework) Added a bank statistics view
  • (Bank Rework) Added a credit rating system (as a fun thing :D)
  • (Bank Rework) You can now turn off the confirmation dialogue
  • (Bank Rework) Added a sorting option to the bank to sort by level requirements
  • (Bank Rework) Added missing attributes to the filters
  • (Bank Rework) Added a filter for travelling
  • (Bank Rework) Added a button to filters to clear all
  • (Bank Rework) Added a filter for rare pet eggs
  • (Bank Rework) Added a filter to only show the highest quality gear/tool items
  • (Bank Rework) Added a context option for category headers to copy a category
  • (Bank Rework) Added the skill group icons (gathering, artisan, utility) to the icon picker
  • (Bank Rework) Added an option to lock items inside a category
  • (Bank Rework) Added an option to the bank settings to lock items inside all categories that have no filters
  • (Keywords) "Hunting product" keyword
  • (Keywords) "Curiosity" keyword

Changed

  • (Bank Rework) While dragging stuff in bank, the drag overlay object is now smaller and offset so you can see better
  • Loosened up the pet name profanity filter a bit
  • AP from achievements is now only gained once the achievement has been claimed

Fixed

  • (Bank Rework) Fixed the categories not being highlighted when you drag something to them
  • (Bank Rework) With filters, sorting or search active, you can now also drag items straight to the category body instead of just the header
  • (Bank Rework) Fixed icons being a big offset in the icon picker for tabs and categories
  • (Bank Rework) More improvements to the search bar open/close speed when something is written there already
  • (Bank Rework) Deposit from inventory etc. should now also update most recent tab
  • (Bank Rework) Searching for rare pet eggs with 'Rare' should now work
  • (Bank Rework) Applied some improvements to the bank search, so for instance toolbox no longer returns all tools
  • (Bank Rework) Fixed the slight offset in bank grid for item sprites
  • (Bank Rework) Fixed the performance when expanding/collapsing keyboard with search text written to the search bar
  • (Bank Rework) Fixed the incorrect background color preview when creating categories
  • (Bank Rework) Fixed the attribute filters not being applied properly to consumables in the bank
  • (Bank Rework) Applied a fix for foldables and tablets where in the new bank the item icons will scale to 2x once there is enough width and that the grid cells are capped to certain vertical height
  • (Bank Rework) Fixed the rubber banding effect when collapsing the side bar in bank with grid mode enabled
  • You can now deposit in places that only have a deposit service (Horn of Respite)
  • Optimized the step history uploads
  • Fixed the problem when withdrawing rings of different quality with a gear set where it only withdrew the highest quality one
  • Optimizations to the tag texts in the game
  • Applied some optimizations to the inventory view
  • Optimized code for adding items and dropping items
  • Fixed the issue with Map of Arenum attributes not getting properly calculated
  • Applied some optimizations to the WalkScape main view (character, location, activity, journal, abilities view)
  • Renaming the current pet now correctly updates the name in the abilities view card
  • Fixed the bug in reordering gear sets where after dragging the option jumped one above where they should have
  • Fixed the ability timers not resetting if you see them go to 0 while unless you leave the page
  • Fixed the crafting level up counter not adding up correctly
  • Fixed the opening chest spinner re-appearing after teleporting
  • Fixed the collectibles count lagging one behind until restarting the game
  • Fixed the AP from collectibles lagging one behind (and same for lore item counts) until restarting the game
  • Optimized local storage reads and writes for better performance
  • Optimized game-data load: object insertion now uses the known data type instead of re-detecting it, and object lookups by id use a flat index instead of scanning every type bucket
  • Main view pages (journal, activity, character, location, abilities) now remember their scroll position while switching between them
  • Implemented small optimization to game data initialization
  • (Items) Bones, Feather, Dark feather, Lizard tail, Animal meat, Animal fur, Aerodynamic thread, Hide scraps, Basic hide, Elder hide, and Unicorn horn now have the "Hunting product" keyword
  • (Items) Unidentified remains, Adventurers' enamel pin, Name tag, Halfmaw teeth, and Halfmaw scales now have the "Curiosity" keyword
  • (Achievements) All The Things I Could Do unlock requirement changed to have a total wealth of 100k
  • (Achievements) Time To Party unlock requirement changed to have a total wealth of 1m

WalkScape:_Grind_by_walking!.title: WalkScape: Grind by walking!
WalkScape:_Grind_by_walking!.html:
WalkScape is a game heavily inspired by classic point and click MMORPGs. But instead of playing actively, you gain progress by walking in real life. It's designed to be non-intrusive, with no predatory monetization practices. By non-intrusive we mean that it will truly let you enjoy your time outside by not constantly requiring your attention. Everything that needs active involvement (like combat or quests) should be done when you get home. The main goal of the game is to make people more interested in walking by giving them an amazing gaming experience to motivate them to keep walking. And you can play it while at work, or when you are walking with friends, and while walking your dog. You can truly focus on what you are doing and do more active playing later.

Before getting started with the game, please familiarize yourself with the Rules and make sure your device is compatible with the System Requirements.


SkillsItemsLocations
Skills are leveled up while doing activities related to the skill. They unlock you new content and make you more efficient.Items are objects that can be collected, used, or sold. They can be found in the world, bought from vendors, or crafted by players.Locations are places in the world that can be visited. They provide services and activities for your character to engage with.
ActivitiesKeywordsServices
Activities are repeating tasks that can be done in the world by walking in real life. They are the main way to get items and level up your skills.Keywords are used on many items, locations, services and activities. You can easily check from here for instance which items count as light sources.Services provide you with benefits in a location. Most commonly they enable you to do artisan recipes.
RecipesCharactersBuildings
Recipes are the way to craft items yourself. They usually require materials and a service.Characters are the people you can meet in the world. They can give you quests, sell you items, and more.Buildings are structures in the world that commonly provide you with shops and services such as banking.
Shops
Shops are places where you can buy and sell items. They are usually found in buildings.


We are always looking to improve and correct parts of the wiki's information. We ask for your patience while we keep updating missing pages and info, but if you have anything that you noticed that needs attention - please let us know under the wiki chat section of the Discord! If you are new with questions, we recommend you check the FAQs page to start and the sidebar on the left for some basic WalkScape information you may find useful, and if you'd like to help translate check out the localization page. Thank you, stay hydrated, and keep walking!

What_A_Trip.html:
What A Trip
Type:Normal

Eating some might also take you to a wild trip. Best consumed in good company.

What A Trip is an achievement.

Requirement

  • Forage Mushroom from Plant foraging activities. [300]

Rewards

Achievement Point Rewards:

  • 3x achievement points

Other Rewards:

  • Mushroom companion

Guides

  • This can be done with Spring cave foraging or Summer cave foraging, so it is recommended to have good Gear for Foraging with a light source or two. You can also make progress towards the Winnie the Pooh achievement, although you will likely finish this one before you have enough Honeycomb.
  • There is an activity dependency if you want to do Summer cave foraging:
  • You must complete Spring bat tracking (2 light sources required) to do Summer cave foraging
  • You must complete 10 actions of Spring cave foraging to complete Spring bat tracking

Woodcutting.title: Woodcutting
Woodcutting.html:
Harvest timber from the vast forests of Arenum, yielding raw materials that are essential in the world's industries.

The Woodcuttingskill allows you to gather logs from chopping trees. Logs can be processed into planks with the Carpentry skill. With higher Woodcutting levels, you'll have access to more trees, better hatchets, and special skilling equipment that can boost your woodcutting efficiency. You can also receive Woodcutting Chests and Bird Nests as a rare drop from training this skill.

Activities

The following activities can be done indefinitely without needing materials. Some have equipment requirements or other requirements that need to be satisfied in order to start the activity.

For activities involving two skills, the player is only eligible to earn chests in skills that have actual level requirements.

So, if the activity has a Woodcutting level requirement, it will be eligible to drop Woodcutting Chests. Additionally, activities involving cutting trees have a chance to drop Bird Nests as well.

When performing an activity for a skill, only the primary skill is factored in for the player's equipment bonuses, the "2nd Skill" will also be affected by the equipment attributes based toward the "1st Skill" (IE: +1 Exp will apply to the "2nd Skill" as well).

Work_Efficiency.title: Work Efficiency
Work_Efficiency.html:
Work Efficiency is an attribute that changes the value of work that your steps produce. Positive work efficiency decreases the amount of steps required to complete an action, while negative work efficiency increases the amount of steps required to complete an action.

You may be looking for:

  • All the items with this attribute
  • How the game uses the attribute in calculations.

Work_Efficiency_(Mechanics).title: Work Efficiency (Mechanics)
Work_Efficiency_(Mechanics).html:
Note: The Travelling activity is an exception to these rules and is handled differently. See Travelling (Mechanics) for more information.

Work Efficiency is derived from two sources:

  1. The base increase from gaining levels in the activity's skill.
  2. The increase (or decrease) from any equipped gear or tools.

Work Efficiency Calculation

  1. Each activity has an initial base work per action with 1 work unit equating to 1 step.
  2. The total efficiency is then calculated. - Skills give a +1.25% efficiency bonus for each level over the minimum up to a maximum of 25%. ((Skill Level - Activity Level) × 0.0125) - The equipment bonus is as stated in the details for that item for the relevant skill.
  3. This calculated added efficiency is then compared to the maximum efficiency for the activity. If your efficiency is greater than the maximum, then it is set to be the maximum. - The maximum added efficiency can be found in the Walkpedia entry for that activity.
  4. These bonuses are then added to the base 100% efficiency that you have for every activity. - If your calculated efficiency is negative or zero it is set to a minimum of 1%.
  5. The new work per action is then calculated by taking the base work divided by the efficiency (as a number, not a percent).
  6. The work per action is then rounded up to the nearest full step.

The full formula is:
Adjusted Steps per action = ceiling(max((Base Steps ÷ Work Efficiency), 10))

Example with Minimum Skill Levels Only

If we want to do Hut jumping with an agility level of 25 and no gear.

  1. We look at the base work for the activity. - There is a base work value of 53.00 work units (steps).
  2. We have level 25 agility, and the activity requires level 25 agility. - Level efficiency gain: ((25 Skill Level - 25 Activity Level) × 0.0125) = ((0 Levels over Minimum) × 0.0125) = 0% (0.00) added level efficiency which is lower than the 25% maximum. - Equipment efficiency gain: We have no gear that gives efficiency bonuses. = 0% (0.00) added equipment efficiency - Calculate total added efficiency. 0% level efficiency + 0% equipment efficiency = 0% (0.00) added efficiency
  3. We compare to the maximum efficiency for the activity. - Hut jumping has a maximum efficiency of 50% (0.50) as shown in its Walkpedia entry. - We have a 0% (0.00) added efficiency, so we are below the maximum. - We use the smaller value, so our effective efficiency is 0% (0.00).
  4. We add the level and equipment efficiency to the base efficiency value. - 100% base efficiency + 0% added efficiency = 100% (1.00) total efficiency
  5. We calculate the new work per action for the activity. - 53.00 base work units ÷ 1.00 effective efficiency = 53.00 calculated work per action
  6. We round work per action up to the nearest full step value. - 53.00 calculated work per action rounds up to 53 steps per action.

Example with Skill Levels Over the Minimum

If we want to do Hut jumping with an agility level of 40 and no gear.

  1. We look at the base work for the activity. - There is a base work value of 53.00 work units (steps).
  2. We have level 40 agility, and the activity requires level 25 agility. - Level efficiency gain: ((40 Skill Level - 25 Activity Level) × 0.0125) = ((15 Levels over Minimum) × 0.0125) = 18.75% (0.1875) added level efficiency which is lower than the 25% maximum. - Equipment efficiency gain: We have no gear that gives efficiency bonuses. = 0% (0.00) added equipment efficiency - Calculate total added efficiency. 18.75% level efficiency + 0% equipment efficiency = 18.75% (0.1875) added efficiency
  3. We compare to the maximum efficiency for the activity. - Hut jumping has a maximum efficiency of 50% (0.50) as shown in its Walkpedia entry. - We have a 18.75% (0.1875) added efficiency, so we are below the maximum. - We use the smaller value, so our effective efficiency is 18.75% (0.1875).
  4. We add the level and equipment efficiency to the base efficiency value. - 100% base efficiency + 18.75% added efficiency = 118.75% (1.1875) total efficiency
  5. We calculate the new work per action for the activity. - 53.00 base work units ÷ 1.1875 effective efficiency = 44.63 calculated work per action
  6. We round work per action up to the nearest full step value. - 44.63 calculated work per action rounds up to 45 steps per action.

Example with Skill Levels Over the Minimum and Equipment

If we want to do Hut jumping with an agility level of 40 and a Walking stick.

  1. We look at the base work for the activity. - There is a base work value of 53.00 work units (steps).
  2. We have level 40 agility, and the activity requires level 25 agility. - Level efficiency gain: ((40 Skill Level - 25 Activity Level) × 0.0125) = ((15 Levels over Minimum) × 0.0125) = 18.75% (0.1875) added level efficiency which is lower than the 25% maximum. - Equipment efficiency gain: The Walking stick gives +5.0% work efficiency = 5% (0.05) added equipment efficiency - Calculate total added efficiency. 18.75% level efficiency + 5% equipment efficiency = 23.75% (0.2375) added efficiency
  3. We compare to the maximum efficiency for the activity. - Hut jumping has a maximum efficiency of 50% (0.50) as shown in its Walkpedia entry. - We have a 23.75% (0.2375) added efficiency, so we are below the maximum. - We use the smaller value, so our effective efficiency is 23.75% (0.2375).
  4. We add the level and equipment efficiency to the base efficiency value. - 100% base efficiency + 23.75% added efficiency = 123.75% (1.2375) total efficiency
  5. We calculate the new work per action for the activity. - 53.00 base work units ÷ 1.2375 effective efficiency = 42.83 calculated work per action
  6. We round work per action up to the nearest full step value. - 42.83 calculated work per action rounds up to 43 steps per action.

Example with Efficiency Over the Maximum

If we want to do Hut jumping with an agility level of 40 and items that give a total +50.0% efficiency.

  1. We look at the base work for the activity. - There is a base work value of 53.00 work units (steps).
  2. We have level 50 agility, and the activity requires level 25 agility. - Level efficiency gain: ((50 Skill Level - 25 Activity Level) × 0.0125) = ((25 Levels over Minimum) × 0.0125) = 31.25% (0.3125) added level efficiency which is higher than the 25% maximum so we use 25% as the level efficiency. - Equipment efficiency gain: Our items give a +50.0% efficiency = 50% (0.50) added equipment efficiency - Calculate total added efficiency. 25% level efficiency + 50% equipment efficiency = 75% (0.75) added efficiency
  3. We compare to the maximum efficiency for the activity. - Hut jumping has a maximum efficiency of 50% (0.50) as shown in its Walkpedia entry. - We have a 75% added efficiency, so we are above the maximum. - We use the smaller value, so our effective efficiency is 50%.
  4. We add the level and equipment efficiency to the base efficiency value. - 100% base efficiency + 50% added efficiency = 150% (1.50) total efficiency
  5. We calculate the new work per action for the activity. - 53.00 base work units ÷ 1.50 effective efficiency = 35.33 calculated work per action
  6. We round work per action up to the nearest full step value. - 35.33 calculated work per action rounds up to 36 steps per action.

Note: For Hut jumping 36 steps per action is the minimum possible for this activity from efficiency gains. It is possible to reduce this further from step reduction attributes

Wrentmark.title: Wrentmark
Wrentmark.html:
Wrentmark is a peninsula located just southwest of the rest of Wallisia, connected via the Kildome Cross. It is a realm forged by fire, where the scorching sun beats down upon the desert sands. The people of Wrentmark are a proud and hardy lot, who have thrived in this harsh environment for ages. Wrentmark is a land of untold riches, where precious gems and minerals are mined from the earth and traded across the land. The people of Wrentmark are master merchants, their skills honed through centuries of commerce.

Locations

  • Urban Areas
  • Myriadian Arc
  • Other areas
  • Crown of Cinders
  • Cactus Canyon

Quests

None.

History

Wrentmark, which is rich in gold and other precious minerals, is largely responsible for Wallisia's wealth. Wallisia is largely made up of agriculture and large cities, whereas Wrentmark has mountains and caves filled with riches. Wrentmark has been a source of wealth and power for Wallisia ever since it overcame it, providing the Empire the resources it needs to grow economically and industrially.

As one of the most powerful states in Western Continent, Wrentmark has been under the control of Wallisia for many years. The inhabitants of Wrentmark are proud merchants who are fiercely loyal to their people and consider themselves part of a family-like community. They have a vast appreciation for their own culture and customs, something that is not always shared with those from other parts of the world.

When Wallisia conquered Wrentmark and gained control over its resources and a peace was made, tension immediately began to mount between the two states. Over time, this conflict has become increasingly heated as each sides jockey for power and influence within Wrentmark.

Currently, there is an ongoing power struggle between the Empress and her sons regarding who will succeed her as ruler of Wallisia. Should the succession crisis reach a breaking point, there is a distinct possibility that Wrentmark may secede from Wallisia's rule and return to being an independent state once again. This could lead to further division among realms on the Western Continent, as well as increased conflict between them. Such a situation could have serious implications for future relations between Wallisia and Wrentmark, as well as for peace within the continent at large.

Government and politics

Wrentmark is a minor part of the Western Continent. It was conquered by the Empress's father prior to the construction of the Arena. Its main plot will revolve around its disagreements with the Empress and the gripping rulership of the Wallisian Empire.

Economy

Wrentmark has been a source of wealth and power for Wallisia ever since it overcame it, providing the Empire the resources it needs to grow economically and industrially.

Zeno_Rocca.title: Zeno Rocca
Zeno_Rocca.html:
Zeno Rocca
Location:Jeweled Oasis Bank

An eager looking man serving at the grand bank of the Myriadian Arc. He looks almost as if he has stepped out of a painting with how perfect his style and expression set the scene.

Zeno Rocca is a character who can be found at Jeweled Oasis Bank in Myriadian Arc in the Wrentmark region.

Quote

  • Welcome! Thank you for making your way over to the Jeweled Oasis Bank. Just like our structure itself, we can assure your valued treasures will be kept safe at all times.

Rumor

  • Fleeting feet.
  • Have you ever seen such beautiful boots? I mean Feather boots of course! I heard the shops here were supposed to get some of them, but ships with them crashed over at Kildome Cross along the shoreline. Such a shame.

Home.title: Welcome to WalkScape
Home.html:
WalkScape is a game heavily inspired by classic point and click MMORPGs. But instead of playing actively, you gain progress by walking in real life. It's designed to be non-intrusive, with no predatory monetization practices. By non-intrusive we mean that it will truly let you enjoy your time outside by not constantly requiring your attention. Everything that needs active involvement (like combat or quests) should be done when you get home. The main goal of the game is to make people more interested in walking by giving them an amazing gaming experience to motivate them to keep walking. And you can play it while at work, or when you are walking with friends, and while walking your dog. You can truly focus on what you are doing and do more active playing later.

Before getting started with the game, please familiarize yourself with the Rules and make sure your device is compatible with the System Requirements.

We are always looking to improve and correct parts of the wiki's information. We ask for your patience while we keep updating missing pages and info, but if you have anything that you noticed that needs attention - please let us know under the wiki chat section of the Discord! If you are new with questions, we recommend you check the FAQs page to start and the sidebar on the left for some basic WalkScape information you may find useful, and if you'd like to help translate check out the localization page. Thank you, stay hydrated, and keep walking!
